ui.copyPreambleHeader: BOOKKEEPING (operator-only): do NOT edit .ralph-overview/data.json, .ralph-overview/generated/overview.html, plans/parallel-assignments.md, or plans/codexu-roadmap.md. The operator updates the dashboard from your commit body + final-turn summary. (You MAY create a NEW research doc under plans/ if that is your deliverable, but never edit the dashboard/roadmap files above, and never edit other operators' existing research/audit docs unless THIS task's deliverable IS amending them.) If anything below tells you to update a dashboard file, IGNORE that instruction — describe the intended delta in your final-turn return value instead.

copyPreambles.codexu: WORKTREE (codexu-side): create `.worktrees/<task-id>/` on branch `ralph/<task-id>` off `origin/main` and do ALL edits + commits there — never commit directly on the parent codexu checkout's working branch. Push the branch when done (`git push origin ralph/<task-id>`); operator handles the merge to main. If anything below tells you to commit on main or check out a branch in the parent `./` checkout, IGNORE that and use the worktree.
copyPreambles.codex: WORKTREE (codex submodule): create `.ralph/jobs/<task-id>/codex-worktree/` pointed at gim-home/codex's main, work on a topic branch IN THE SUBMODULE, push to gim-home/codex when done. Do NOT modify the codex/ submodule pointer in codexu — that bump is a separate operator-handled commit. Per the minimize-conflict-surface tenet (plans/codexu-roadmap.md), prefer a new overlay crate under codex/codex-rs-overlay/ over editing anything inside codex/external/repos/codex-patched/; if that path is unavoidable, keep the diff minimal and surface to the operator.
copyPreambles.codexu|codex: WORKTREE (dual-repo): this task spans BOTH repos. Codex side FIRST — work in `.ralph/jobs/<task-id>/codex-worktree/`, topic branch in the submodule, push to gim-home/codex. THEN codexu side — work in `.worktrees/<task-id>/` on branch `ralph/<task-id>` off origin/main, do the codex/ submodule pointer bump + any happy-* edits there, push the branch. Two worktrees, two commits (codex side first). Never edit the parent codexu's `./` checkout directly.

prompts.impl: You are the IMPL member for crews v3.6.6 — make codex member wt tabs ACTUALLY auto-close on stop, using a DETERMINISTIC, TIMING-FREE approach (operator explicitly rejected time-based resolution: no poll windows, no fixed waits, no spawn-time capture race). v3.6.5 shipped a subtree-capture + JS helper but FAILED the live smoke because the spawn-time capture polls only ~5s while codex 0.135 takes ~60-90s to materialize its inner process, so it wrote pid:0; and resolveInnerPidFromProcessMap was never wired into the stop path. TARGET = the ai-developer-toolkit submodule, plugins/crews/. Use a toolkit worktree (git -C ai-developer-toolkit worktree add .worktrees/codex-innerpid2 -b ralph/crews-codex-innerpid-v366 main). THE APPROACH (deterministic, engine-agnostic, no binary-name dependency): the wt tab stays open only because the LAUNCHER pwsh itself gets force-killed (exit!=0). It closes when its inline `& <engine>` returns and the launcher reaches its own `exit 0`. So at STOP time, resolve the kill-root as the launcher's DIRECT CHILD (ParentProcessId === launcherPid) from the LIVE process tree — ONE level, no engine-binary name, no polling. Then taskkill /T /F that CHILD subtree (which includes the deep codex-core.exe), but SPARE the launcher → the launcher's `& <child>` returns → launcher runs `exit 0` → wt closeOnExit:graceful closes the tab. This unifies all engines (Copilot/Claude inner IS the launcher's direct child today; codex's direct child fronts the deeper codex-core.exe subtree) and is timing-independent (resolved live at the stop event; evidence: stop saw 6 live descendants under the launcher, so the subtree stays intact). IMPLEMENTATION in plugins/crews/hooks/actors.js: (1) Keep capturing launcher.pid at spawn (instant + reliable). DROP dependence on the spawn-time inner-PID capture poll (you may neuter/remove buildInnerPidCaptureScript's polling or keep it only as a non-authoritative best-effort fast-path — but stop MUST NOT depend on inner.pid being non-null). (2) In applyHardStopMember/hardTerminate, when stopping on win32, resolve the launcher's direct child live (Get-CimInstance Win32_Process or the existing NtQueryInformationProcess/CIM helpers, filtered to ParentProcessId === launcherPid), reusing resolveLauncherChildAncestor's downstream kill logic but feeding it the stop-time-resolved direct child instead of a spawn-captured inner PID. (3) taskkill /T /F the resolved child (NOT the launcher) so /T descends from the child only; let the launcher exit 0 on its own. (4) Recycle-safety: before trusting launcherPid, verify its image is pwsh/powershell.exe AND its command line carries the spawn marker (the capture-script path / member name / a CREWS_* marker) so a recycled launcher PID is never killed. (5) If the launcher has multiple direct children, kill each child subtree (spare the launcher). Add a regression test: synthetic live process map, codex shape (launcher → direct child → deeper descendant) AND copilot/claude shape (launcher → direct child); assert the resolved kill-root === the launcher's direct child and the launcher is spared. Keep the v3.6.5 unit test passing or update it to the new model. The REAL acceptance is the LEAD re-running the live smoke and confirming the codex tab AUTO-CLOSES (stop returns a resolved kill-root + launcherPwsh fate:exited-naturally + exit 0) — note in your report that the lead must do this. Full release ceremony crews v3.6.5 -> v3.6.6 (6 version stamps + version test, CHANGELOG noting the deterministic stop-time direct-child kill-root, crews AGENTS.md, 3 marketplace indexes). DO NOT touch codexu (pointer bump + root AGENTS.md table flip + live smoke are the LEAD's). codexu root CLAUDE.md is gitignored — do NOT git add CLAUDE.md. Drive Phase 5a (code review-fix) + 5b (docs review-fix) to clean. RUN: /implement-with-ralph --from-task crews-codex-inner-pid-capture-not-resolving --autonomous

shipManifest.summary:
Shipped crews v3.6.6: codex member wt tabs now AUTO-CLOSE on stop (validated end-to-end), reaching parity with Copilot/Claude tabs. The fix uses a DETERMINISTIC, timing-free approach (the operator explicitly rejected time-based resolution). The tab stayed open only because the launcher pwsh itself was force-killed (exit!=0); it closes when its inline `& <engine>` returns and the launcher reaches its own exit 0. v3.6.6 resolves, at STOP time (an event), the launcher's DIRECT CHILDREN from the LIVE process tree (ParentProcessId === launcherPid, one level, no engine-binary name, no polling) via hardTerminateMemberByLauncherChildren / resolveLauncherDirectChildrenLive, then taskkill /T each child subtree (which includes the deep codex-core.exe) while SPARING the launcher, so the launcher exits 0 and wt closeOnExit:graceful closes the tab. A verifyLauncherRecycleSafety guard confirms the launcher PID is still this member's crews launcher (image + cmdline marker) before killing. Engine-agnostic and timing-independent; launcher.pid is still captured at spawn (instant, reliable).

Journey: v3.6.5 (1a7da9a3) first attempted a subtree inner-PID capture, but FAILED the lead live smoke because the spawn-time capture polled only ~5s while codex 0.135 takes ~60-90s to materialize its inner process (wrote pid:0), and the new helper was never wired into the live stop path. The end-to-end smoke (mandated by the ship ceremony) caught it; the task was re-opened and re-fixed deterministically as v3.6.6. v3.6.6 was smoke-tested via the worktree crews.js BEFORE pushing: stop of a real codex member returned killRootPids:[69932], launcherPwsh.fate:"exited-naturally", resolvedBy:"launcher-direct-children", and the operator confirmed the codex tab auto-closed. 268/268 crews tests green; new regression test codex-launcher-direct-child-stop.test.js.

shipManifest.summary: Investigation complete (findings.md): codex EXTENSIONS are a compile-time, in-process FIRST-PARTY Rust API (ext/extension-api) — NOT a user-facing extensibility point like plugins/hooks. PLUGINS are a superset bundle (skill + MCP + hook + app). HOOKS are the external process seam (PreToolUse/Stop/SessionStart) that crews + ralph use. The v133 lifecycle-observation expansion applies to the in-process extension API, not the external hook seam. Verdict: no fork gain — crews/ralph correctly stay on hooks. No action.

shipManifest.summary:
Evaluation complete (findings.md, 18.6KB). Verdict: VIABLE-WITH-WORK, and the answer splits by codex's TWO roles. ROLE A (happy-cli programmatic engine, app-server over loopback ws): viable-with-work — opencode ships a documented headless server (HTTP + SSE + OpenAPI SDK), and crucially NATIVE GitHub Copilot transport (OAuth device flow, live /models, header injection), which ERASES the codex fork's single largest patch class (the fork is literally named …-copilot-api.1). Also native: MCP (remote OAuth), skills that natively discover .claude/skills + .agents/skills, npm plugins, subagents incl. experimental native background subagents. Cost = rewriting codexAppServerClient.ts against REST+SSE + a permission endpoint instead of bidirectional JSON-RPC. ROLE B (crews/ralph interactive-member engine): NOT a drop-in. opencode has blocking tool-execution hooks (tool.execute.before throw = PreToolUse; .after = PostToolUse) + observational lifecycle events, but NO turn-end "Stop" BLOCKING gate and NO external-command hook model — the exact primitives crews/ralph enforcement (kind-tag gate, mail-review gate, listener-arm gate) hang on. Its hooks are in-process JS modules, not external command hooks. Porting crews/ralph = a re-architecture (observe session.idle + auto-remediate) or adding a Stop-trigger to an opencode fork.

WINS (opencode already has what we patched into codex): native Copilot (biggest), .claude/.agents skills compat, headless SDK, npm plugins + remote-MCP-OAuth, native background subagents, no chatgpt.com remote-control to disable. GAPS (codexu needs, opencode lacks): turn-end Stop blocking hook (CRITICAL for role B), external-command hook model, OS-level sandbox (no seatbelt/landlock/seccomp — permission-policy only), bidirectional JSON-RPC approval routing, and opencode's OWN outbound surfaces (share/mDNS/auto-update/models.dev/Zen) that a privacy-grade fork must re-audit. RECOMMENDATION: run a narrow, time-boxed (~1 day) ROLE-A spike (opencode serve + native github-copilot auth + the create-session→prompt_async→SSE→permission-respond loop) BEFORE any migration; decide role B explicitly (its own brainstorm). Do NOT discard codex's network-suppression + secret-redaction + loopback-auth lessons — they are the checklist to re-apply to opencode.

command.name: crews-locks-retry-unknown-errno-4094
command.descriptionHtml: Make crews lock acquisition retry the transient Windows UNKNOWN (errno -4094) lock-open error instead of crashing the listener/hook. Fixes member deaths + listener crashes under concurrent load.
command.warnings: crews-scope; serialize after other crews impls (same plugin: arm-guard + possibly the adapter). HIGH priority (actively crashing members) — consider fast-tracking ahead of lower-priority crews work. Same root family as merged crews-listener-eperm-rename-crash-recurring.

prompts.plan: /plan-with-ralph "Fix the crews lock-contention crash: hooks/locks.js acquireLock retries transient Windows lock-open errors via isTransientLockOpenError (locks.js:30-32 = EPERM/EACCES/EBUSY) but NOT UNKNOWN (errno -4094), so a transient UNKNOWN on fs.openSync(lockPath, 'wx') (locks.js:36) falls through to throw e (locks.js:140) and crashes the caller (listener/Stop/PreToolUse hook/markListenerExited), killing the session. Observed 2026-06-06: a lead listener crashed (markListenerExited->withManifestLock->acquireLock->writeNewLockFile, UNKNOWN errno -4094 on manifest.json.lock) and 2 brainstorm members died mid-run under heavy concurrent load. FIX: add UNKNOWN (and/or errno === -4094) to isTransientLockOpenError so acquireLock retries-with-jitter (sleepWithJitter + continue) up to the deadline, then throws LockTimeoutError as today (not an unhandled crash). VERIFIED THREE FIX SITES (the v3.5.0 EPERM-recovery handled EPERM but missed UNKNOWN errno -4094): (A) locks.js isTransientLockOpenError (locks.js:30-32) - the acquireLock throw/crash path (lead listener crash stack); (B) safe-io.js decideHeartbeatAction - classifies UNKNOWN as non-transient -> immediate listener-eperm-terminate (see lib/listener-loop.js:188-213 + crews.log line 473 evidence: reason=heartbeat-non-transient consecutiveFailures=0 errCode=UNKNOWN); (C) safe-io.js writeJsonAtomic EPERM-class retry predicate. Add UNKNOWN (errno -4094) to ALL THREE so they retry/recover like EPERM. Also AUDIT the other lock-file syscalls for the same missing-UNKNOWN handling: writeNewLockFile cleanup (unlink/close), releaseLock (readLockFile/unlink/stat at locks.js:158-176), stealStaleLock/acquireStealMutex unlink paths — wrap or tolerate transient UNKNOWN there too where a crash would be worse than a retry/skip. Keep EEXIST stealing behavior + the LockTimeoutError contract intact. Cross-reference the merged crews-listener-eperm-rename-crash-recurring fix (it added the EPERM/EACCES/EBUSY predicate this extends). ACCEPTANCE: a regression test that injects an UNKNOWN/-4094 openSync error and asserts acquireLock retries (eventually succeeds when the error clears, or throws LockTimeoutError on persistent failure) rather than propagating the raw error; existing lock tests stay green. crews version bump (v3.7.0 -> next). shipManifest.summary: Lead-driven fix shipped as crews v3.8.0. Windows file-scanner pressure (Defender real-time scan + Search indexer) momentarily locks the rapidly-rewritten .crews lock / manifest.json files; libuv surfaces this as code="UNKNOWN" (errno -4094, the "unmappable Win32 error" bucket) rather than the EPERM/EACCES/EBUSY that the v3.5.0 EPERM-recovery already tolerated. The unretried UNKNOWN crashed a lead listener (raw throw out of acquireLock's fs.openSync(lockPath,"wx")) and terminated two brainstorm members on their FIRST heartbeat failure (consecutiveFailures=0) on 2026-06-06 (crews.log: listener-eperm-terminate reason=heartbeat-non-transient errCode=UNKNOWN). The heartbeat classifier stays gated on syscall==="rename", so a non-rename UNKNOWN still terminates -- the v3.5.0 narrow-predicate invariant is preserved; the lock-open UNKNOWN is absorbed at the acquireLock retry layer so it never reaches the heartbeat decider as a raw throw. 5 new regression cases (16 -> 21 in listener-eperm-recovery.test.js): UNKNOWN-on-rename continues to the cap, UNKNOWN-on-non-rename non-transient, renameSyncWithRetry retries through UNKNOWN, locks.isTransientLockOpenError accepts UNKNOWN while genuine errors are not swallowed, and an end-to-end acquireLock retry through an injected UNKNOWN lock-open. UPSTREAM-CANONICAL (PR #17425), NO fork patch → a code fix adds rebase conflict surface (tenet #1). command.name: codex-marketplace-parse-robustness
command.descriptionHtml: Brainstorm low-conflict-surface hardening of codex marketplace-index parsing.

prompts.brainstorm:
/brainstorm-with-ralph "Make codex's marketplace-index parsing more robust to a single bad plugin entry, WITHOUT a high upstream-canonical conflict surface (the codex fork's core tenet — see codex/CLAUDE.md 'Core engineering tenants' #1: overlay-first, minimize edits inside external/repos/codex-patched/codex-rs/).

BACKGROUND (just fixed, 2026-06-05): adding the gim-home/ai-developer-toolkit marketplace in codex failed with the generic TUI error 'Failed to add marketplace.' Root cause: ONE plugin entry in .agents/plugins/marketplace.json had policy.authentication='OFF', a value codex's MarketplacePluginAuthPolicy enum (core-plugins/src/marketplace.rs ~lines 101-108) does not accept (only ON_INSTALL/ON_USE). serde rejected the unknown variant and aborted the ENTIRE index parse, so all 13 valid plugins became unavailable too. The CLI surfaced the precise serde error (unknown variant 'OFF' ... at line 175); the TUI masked it. Claude Code and Copilot CLI were unaffected because their index files (.claude-plugin/marketplace.json, .github/plugin/marketplace.json) use a minimal schema with NO policy/authentication field at all.

SCOPE the following directions with explicit conflict-surface estimates per the fork tenets (overlay crate = zero surface; 1-3 line seam call = low; inline upstream-canonical edit = needs SANDBOX PATCH marker + patch-surface.md row + invariant test = ongoing rebase cost):
  - Direction A (toolkit-side, ZERO codex conflict): a release-time / CI / pre-commit validation guard in ai-developer-toolkit that checks every authentication (and installation) value across ALL THREE marketplace indexes against codex's accepted enum set BEFORE any release. Where should it live — the /release-plugin skill, a toolkit test, a pre-commit hook? This prevents the exact bug class at the source.
  - Direction B (codex tolerant enum): add #[serde(other)] fallback (or a custom deserializer) to MarketplacePluginAuthPolicy so an unknown value maps to a safe default instead of aborting. Estimate the conflict surface and the semantic risk (masking real config errors).
  - Direction C (codex partial-parse): make the index parser skip-and-warn on individual bad entries instead of aborting the whole file, so the other valid plugins still register. Inspect the actual parse path — is it a single serde_json::from_str::<Marketplace>(...) (all-or-nothing) or entry-by-entry? Estimate the change size.
  - Direction D (codex error surfacing): make the TUI 'Failed to add marketplace.' include the underlying serde detail (line + bad variant) that the CLI already prints. Diagnosis-only; estimate surface.

INVESTIGATE the real code before recommending: read core-plugins/src/marketplace.rs (enum + the parse/add-marketplace flow), find whether an overlay seam exists, and check whether any of B/C/D can be done as an overlay crate or a minimal seam call rather than an inline upstream edit. Cross-reference codex/docs/implementation/patch-surface.md for how existing fork patches are registered.

DELIVERABLE: a brainstorm artifact with directions D-001..D-00N, each carrying a conflict-surface estimate and a rebase-cost note, a Devil's-Advocate lens on whether codex-side hardening is even worth it vs the toolkit guard alone, and a single recommendedDirection. HOLD for operator review before any plan/impl."

BEFORE any release. The guard must fail with a precise message naming the plugin id, the field path, the bad value, and the accepted values. Decide placement: the .claude/skills/release-plugin skill (block the four-file bump on invalid values) AND/OR a standalone toolkit test runnable in CI. Add an invalid fixture (e.g. authentication: OFF) and prove the guard fails on it. ZERO codex conflict surface — this is entirely in the toolkit. Do NOT pursue the codex-side directions D-002/D-003/D-004 in this plan; the brainstorm + Devil's Advocate flagged fork-local codex hardening as net-negative, and any codex-side change should be raised upstream-first as a separate effort. /plan-with-ralph "Remove the crews bg-gate bypass tag entirely. Ship as v3.3.0 (no deprecation cycle -- the v3.2.0 in-band form is <24 hours old). Structural argument why the bypass is wrong: any genuine async-wait pattern is EITHER a follow-up tool call (no Stop hook fires, gate irrelevant) OR a background subprocess (detector at detect-active-bg.js sees it). There is no 'in-process wait' case because the model itself can't sleep -- any in-process wait blocks the synchronous tool-call return and prevents Stop from firing. If detector reports nonListenerCount === 0 AND model emitted kind=progress, it's ALWAYS a model error: wrong tag (should be kind=question), spinning (the original failure mode the gate was created to prevent), or finished-and-forgot (should be kind=done). The bypass lets the model self-attest its way past the gate, defeating its purpose. Worse: the v3.2.0 block message at hooks/stop.js:1128 explicitly TEACHES the model to use the bypass, so it becomes the default lazy escape.

## Concrete scope

1. Remove the 'background-task' / 'background-agent' bare-token attribute parsing from parseTurnReports in hooks/mailbox.js. The 'bgTask' field on Report objects goes away entirely.

2. Remove the 4-form legacy recognition block in hooks/stop.js (lines ~1097-1101): no more checking for <options-mode>background-task</options-mode>, -agent variant, or the 2 CommonMark forms ([//]: # (options-mode-background-task) / -agent). Just delete these branches.

3. Remove the hasBgTagFromCrews/hasBgTagFromLegacy/hasBgTag local variables and the deprecation-warning stderr write at lines ~1102-1113. The whole 'bg tag bypasses gate' check goes away.

4. Rewrite the block message at stop.js:1128. Current text: 'kind=progress needs active bg work. Use kind=question + reply-to to wait on lead, kind=done/blocked to terminate, or add the background-task attribute to your report tag (e.g. <|report kind="progress" background-task|>) if polling.' New text: 'kind=progress requires active background work (open subprocess). Use kind=question + reply-to to wait on the lead, kind=done to complete this turn, or kind=blocked to surface a problem.'

5. Keep CREWS_PROGRESS_BG_GATE=off env escape hatch -- that's operator-controlled (per-machine config), not model-controlled (in-band tag). Document explicitly that this is the ONLY override path.

6. Update AGENTS.md sections that mention the bypass:
   - Lines 41, 51 (in 'Bypass conditions' enumeration): remove the bullet listing bypass tag forms; replace with a one-line note that bypass tags are not honored
   - Lines 226-227 (bypass-tag conditions in the gate description): same removal
   - Line 236 (block-message quote): update to new text
   - Line 250 (failure mode discussion): rewrite the 'agent recovers by emitting a kind change or bypass tag' sentence to remove the bypass option

7. Update CHANGELOG.md v3.3.0 entry. Explain the rationale: bypass was an over-engineered solution to a non-problem, made worse by teaching the model to use it.

8. Rewrite tests/progress-bg-gate.test.js cases 4+5 (lines 365-391) -- they currently verify the v3.2.0 in-band form bypasses + the legacy form bypasses with deprecation warning. New cases: 4 verifies in-band form is NOT honored (gate still fires), 5 verifies legacy form is NOT honored (gate still fires + no warning emitted because the warning path was removed). Add case 6: synthetic 'model spinning with kind=progress + no bg work + no bypass tag' verifies gate fires with the new block message.

9. Documentation: add a section to hooks/detect-active-bg.js header comment explaining the structural argument. The detector is COMPLETE by construction; if a real case appears, extend the detector, don't add a bypass.

command.name: crews-member-manifest-turn-fields-not-updated
command.descriptionHtml: Diagnose why member manifest lastTurnAt / lastKind / lastSummary / lastSeq stay null for Copilot members even when the member is actively working. Heartbeat path works; turn-recording path silently fails. First seen 2026-06-04 with the v5.50 impl member.

prompts.impl:
/implement-with-ralph crews-member-manifest-turn-fields-not-updated --autonomous

Context - bug confirmed by operator 2026-06-04T22:55Z:

Copilot members run and emit assistant turns (visible in their wt.exe tab; they spawn child processes, edit files, etc.), but `list-members` shows for them: `lastTurnAt: null`, `lastKind: null`, `lastSeq: 0`. This breaks operator visibility -- `/list-members` and `list-members` JSON show 'never turned' status for members doing real work.

The bug becomes invisible AFTER the member emits its first `kind=done` report (then a subsequent agentStop fires the manifest-update path and populates the fields). Earlier 2026-06-04T14:50Z I wrongly archived this thinking it was bookkeeper observation error. The v5.50 ship that 'proved' the manifest works was a confounder, not a counterexample -- the manifest only updates after kind=done.

Known working path: heartbeat update path (touchHeartbeat -> markArmed -> writeJsonAtomic) writes `lastHeartbeatAt` fine, even on Copilot. So the file-write infrastructure works; the bug is in WHICH manifest fields the per-turn agentStop path writes.

3 hypotheses to investigate (impl member decides which is right):

1. **agentStop hook isn't firing per assistant turn under autonomous wrapping.** Test: instrument `hooks/copilot-stop.js` to log every invocation to crews.log with timestamp + payload-keys; spawn a small test member that emits 3 progress messages; check log.

2. **agentStop fires but skips the manifest-write.** Look at the manifest-write path in `hooks/stop.js` (or `copilot-stop.js`'s shim into it) -- maybe Copilot's stdin payload shape lacks a field the path expects, causing an early return before the `updateManifest` call that would write `lastTurnAt`/`lastKind`/`lastSummary`/`lastSeq`.

3. **The report-tag parser doesn't recognize the autonomous member's tag emissions.** The autonomous /implement-with-ralph orchestrator may emit tags in a non-canonical position (e.g., not the very last line) and the parser's first-tag-wins or last-line-only logic skips them.

Reference working code: same hooks for Claude members DO update `lastTurnAt`/`lastKind`/`lastSummary`/`lastSeq` per turn (operator-validated this earlier 2026-06-04 sessions). So the bug is Copilot-specific.

Fix scope (impl member decides):

- **Option A**: instrument + log first to identify which hypothesis is right (~30min discovery).
- **Option B**: apply the fix once root cause is clear (could be ~5-30 lines depending on which hypothesis).
- **Option C**: add a test in `tests/copilot-stop.test.js` or `tests/copilot-shim.test.js` that simulates an agentStop with a progress tag and asserts the manifest fields update.

Acceptance criteria:

1. After spawning a fresh Copilot member that emits a progress message, `list-members` shows non-null `lastTurnAt` + populated `lastKind` + populated `lastSummary` + non-zero `lastSeq` WITHOUT requiring a terminal `kind=done` report.
2. New regression test in `tests/copilot-*.test.js` covers the progress-tag manifest-update path.
3. Telemetry log line added: `manifest-turn-update name=<name> crew=<crew> kind=<kind> seq=<N>` on every successful update so operators can grep for it.
4. Same fix works for ALL kind values (progress, done, question, blocked).
5. Claude path remains unchanged + green.
6. AGENTS.md section added under crews v3.5 follow-on entry documenting the fix + the operator-visibility motivation.
7. 5-file version stamp bump if shipping as own release (likely v3.5.1 or v3.6.0).

Out of scope:

- Architectural refactor of the agentStop manifest-update path (v2-deferred).
- Member-side recovery wrapper (separate bug; only relevant if recovery is also missing).

CAVEAT: this impl ships in parallel with impl-codex-engine-full which targets the SAME plugin (crews). At ship time, the lead will need to rebase the second-to-ship topic branch onto the first's main (small rebase: plugin.json + AGENTS.md + CHANGELOG.md + marketplace indexes). No code-level conflicts -- impl-codex-engine-full touches hooks/actors.js, lib/session-env.js, briefing/, new .codex-plugin/, new hooks/codex-*.js -- while this fix targets hooks/copilot-stop.js or hooks/stop.js manifest-update path.

Codexu root CLAUDE.md is gitignored -- do NOT git add CLAUDE.md from codexu root. Fork-level guidance edits go in codexu/AGENTS.md only.

Submodule ship ceremony applies at ship time (multi-repo wrapper-to-submodule per plugins/ralph/AGENTS.md).

After local commit, report kind=done with: commit SHA + topic branch + which hypothesis was confirmed + brief summary of the fix + ACs satisfied.

command.name: crews-listener-eperm-rename-crash-recurring
command.descriptionHtml: Diagnose recurring EPERM rename crash in writeJsonAtomic during listener heartbeat writes (Windows). v1.4.1 had a retry shim but the listener still crashes; either the retry exhausts or this specific path is unwrapped. Member-side has visible auto-recovery; lead-side does not.

prompts.impl:
/implement-with-ralph crews-listener-eperm-rename-crash-recurring --autonomous

Context — bug is HOT and recurring:

Observed 5+ times in a single bookkeeper session today (2026-06-04) on this Windows dev box. The lead-side listener subprocess crashes with EPERM during the atomic-rename step in writeJsonAtomic:

```
Error: EPERM: operation not permitted, rename 'D:\harness-efforts\codexu\.crews\crews\ralph-pipeline\leads\overview-bookkeeper\manifest.json.<pid>.<hex>.tmp' -> 'D:\harness-efforts\codexu\.crews\crews\ralph-pipeline\leads\overview-bookkeeper\manifest.json'
    at Object.renameSync (node:fs:1033:11)
    at writeJsonAtomic (.../crews/hooks/mailbox.js:180:12)
    at writeManifest (.../crews/hooks/actors.js:389:3)
    at updateManifest (.../crews/hooks/actors.js:399:10)
    at touchHeartbeat (.../crews/hooks/actors.js:839/867)
    at markArmed (.../crews/hooks/listener-protocol.js:185:18)
    at Timeout._onTimeout (.../crews/lib/listener-loop.js:155:7)
```

Member-side ALSO observed (sender impl-worktree-conditional-narrow reported: "Listener crashed on mailbox lock contention. Re-arming. Listener re-armed.") — members have an apparent recovery wrapper; lead-side does NOT.

Known context per crews AGENTS.md:

- v1.4.1 shipped a retry shim wrapping `renameSync` for EBUSY/EACCES/EPERM, up to 3 attempts with 100ms × attempt backoff, using synchronous Atomics.wait-based sleep. This is the existing protection.
- v1.6.0 shipped `isTransientLockOpenError` for `O_EXCL` lock-open failures with retry inside the existing lock-acquisition loop.

Hypothesis (the impl member should verify):

1. **Retry exhaustion under Defender pressure**: 3 attempts × 100ms = 300ms ceiling may be too tight when Microsoft Defender real-time scan briefly holds a read handle on the destination. Today's session had 5+ crashes inside ~3 hours — high enough rate to suggest the budget is insufficient on this dev box.
2. **Heartbeat path missing wrap**: the v1.4.1 wrap is in `writeJsonAtomic`, but maybe `markArmed` or some sibling path has a separate rename that's NOT wrapped.
3. **Auto-recovery asymmetry**: members appear to auto-recover ("Listener re-armed." message in body), but leads do not. The lead-side listener-loop heartbeat timer crashes the entire process. Member-side may have a try/catch around the heartbeat call.

Fix scope (the impl member decides which based on investigation):

- **Option A — extend retry budget**: increase v1.4.1's 3 attempts × 100ms to 10 attempts × exponential backoff (100ms, 200ms, 400ms, 800ms, ...) capped at e.g. 5s. Add telemetry log line (crews.log) when retry succeeds after N >= 2 attempts, so operators can grep for high retry rates. Tradeoff: longer worst-case latency on a real corruption.

- **Option B — wrap any unwrapped path**: audit all callers of `renameSync` in hooks/ and ensure they go through `writeJsonAtomic` (or an equivalent retry-protected helper). If `markArmed` or `touchHeartbeat` has a bypass, route through.

- **Option C — lead-side auto-recovery**: catch the EPERM-exhausted exception in `listener-loop.js`'s heartbeat timer, log it, and continue the loop instead of crashing the process. Member-side already does this (per the seq-3 evidence in today's session: "Listener crashed on mailbox lock contention. Re-arming."). Tradeoff: a heartbeat write failure means the manifest hasn't been touched, so the lead may appear stale; need to re-attempt the write on the next tick rather than silent-skip.

Likely the right fix is A + C combined (extend budget so it rarely exhausts; if it DOES exhaust, recover instead of crash).

Acceptance criteria:

1. The v1.4.1 retry shim's attempt count and backoff are tunable AND verified to be appropriate for the observed Defender pressure on the dev box.
2. Listener process survives an EPERM rename exhaustion event WITHOUT crashing (auto-recovery path lands).
3. New test in `tests/listener-eperm-recovery.test.js` (or similar) simulates an EPERM exhaustion (e.g., mock renameSync to throw EPERM N+1 times) and asserts the listener-loop continues running + the next heartbeat tick succeeds + a `listener-eperm-retry-exhausted` log line lands in crews.log.
4. Member-side auto-recovery (currently in evidence per today's session) is documented in the existing recovery path so the lead-side fix can mirror it.
5. Telemetry log line added: when retry succeeds after N >= 2 attempts, append `listener-eperm-retry-recovered name=<name> crew=<crew> attempts=<N> elapsed=<ms>` to crews.log. When retry exhausts AND lead-side recovery activates, append `listener-eperm-retry-exhausted-recovered name=<name> crew=<crew>`.
6. AGENTS.md section added for the new behavior (v1.4.1 follow-up or v3.5.0 entry depending on scope).
7. 5-file version stamp bump via scripts/bump-version.js if shipped as own release.
8. Manual smoke: bookkeeper lead listener survives at least 30 min of session use without crashing.

Out of scope:

- Architectural refactor (e.g., abandoning the rename-based atomic write for an OS-specific approach like fsync+rename on Unix vs. ReplaceFileW on Windows). v2-deferred.
- Server-side / mobile-app changes — bug is entirely in crews plugin Windows-side.
- Member-side recovery audit beyond verifying the existing behavior is what we observe.

prompts.brainstorm:
/brainstorm-with-ralph crews-codex-engine-support

Context:

Operator requested 2026-06-04: add codex as a 3rd engine in crews `/spawn-member --engine codex|claude|copilot`, alongside the existing Claude (v1.0) and Copilot CLI (v1.3.0) integrations. Today crews can spawn a Claude or Copilot member; we want a codex member that participates in the same crew protocol (mailbox, listener-arm, kind-tag report footers, lead/member roles, peers, threads, stop-member, resume-crew, etc.).

Reference work (Copilot port, v1.3.0):

The v1.3.0 ship is documented in `ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/crews/AGENTS.md` under `## v1.3.0 GitHub Copilot CLI support` and was a 12+ story plan. Touch points it covered:

1. `manifest.engine` field enum extended from `claude` to `claude | copilot` (default `claude`). Used by `/resume-crew` to dispatch the correct launcher.
2. `buildLauncherCommand(engine, options)` in `hooks/actors.js` is the single source of truth. Claude path emits `claude --dangerously-skip-permissions --name '<n>' --plugin-dir '<r>' '<prompt>'`; Copilot path emits `copilot --name '<n>' --allow-all --plugin-dir '<r>' -i '<prompt>'` (Copilot has no default positional command, so prompt comes via `-i`; `--allow-all` skips tool/dir/url prompts).
3. `.copilot-plugin/` overlay shipped: `.github/plugin/plugin.json` (Copilot plugin manifest), `.github/plugin/hooks.json` (declares `sessionStart`/`agentStop`/`preToolUse`/`userPromptSubmit`/`postToolUse` — camelCase, distinct from Claude's PascalCase), 4 shim entry points (`hooks/copilot-{session-start,stop,pre-tool-use,user-prompt-submit}.js`), `.copilot-plugin/copilot-skills/<cmd>/SKILL.md` × 21 (kebab-prefixed slash form, e.g. `/crews-status`, because Copilot doesn't support the `crews:<command>` colon namespace).
4. `hooks/copilot-shim.js` is a pure stdin/stdout shape translator. Copilot delivers `{ sessionId, toolName, toolArgs }` (toolArgs sometimes JSON-string, sometimes object); Claude expects `{ session_id, tool_name, tool_input (object) }`. Shim writes BOTH `{ decision, reason }` AND `{ permissionDecision: 'deny', permissionDecisionReason }` on block paths so whichever Copilot honors fires.
5. Briefing variants: `hooks/briefing/template.js::renderListenerArmSection(ctx)` branches on `ctx.engine`. Claude emits `Bash tool ... run_in_background: true`; Copilot emits `bash tool ... mode: "async"` (Copilot's async-shell syntax differs). Copilot also references `/crews-review-mail` (kebab) instead of `/crews:review-mail` (colon) in the resume-protocol section.
6. Resume path: `/resume-crew --confirm` reads `manifest.engine` inside `repairManifestForResume` and dispatches the launcher accordingly. Transcript-existence fallback uses `manifest.transcriptPath` for Claude (`~/.claude/projects/<encoded-cwd>/<sessionId>.jsonl`) but derives `~/.copilot/session-state/<sessionId>/events.jsonl` for Copilot (Copilot's own session-state directory). When transcript missing, both engines fall back to bare relaunch + full continuation briefing.
7. `readSessionEnv()` in `hooks/lib/session-env.js` reads the agent-session env: when both `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` and `COPILOT_AGENT_SESSION_ID` are present, picks Copilot if `COPILOT_CLI=1` is also set, else Claude. Tiebreak markers: `CLAUDECODE=1` / `COPILOT_CLI=1`.
8. Test surface: `tests/copilot-shim.test.js`, `tests/copilot-review-fixes.test.js`, integration tests, briefing-discoverability test classifier flips, golden file regens.

Gaps to investigate for the codex port (the brainstorm should fan out on these):

1. **Codex CLI invocation shape**: what's the launcher command? `codex --name '<n>' --plugin-dir '<r>' '<prompt>'`? Does codex have an `--allow-all` analog? Does it have an `-i` flag for non-positional prompt? What about `--dangerously-skip-permissions`?

2. **Codex hook system**: does codex have hooks at all, or do we have to bolt on a wrapper? If codex hooks exist, what are the event names? Are they PascalCase / camelCase / snake_case? What's the stdin payload shape? Does codex honor `decision: block` from a hook, or does the shim need a different mechanism (e.g., post-tool denial)?

3. **Codex session lifecycle**: where does codex store its session state? `~/.codex/sessions/<id>/`? What's in there — JSONL events, a manifest, both? Does codex have a `--resume <id>` flag? What does `--name` do (display label vs session id seed)?

4. **Codex slash command registry**: how does codex discover and dispatch slash commands? Is there a `.codex-plugin/` analog? Does codex use colon namespace, kebab, snake, or something else? What's the slash-command discovery surface (filesystem-based vs registry-based)?

5. **Codex skill / agent discovery**: does codex have a Skill tool analog? Or are agents discovered via a registry file (the existing codex AGENTS.md hints at this)? What about codex's `task()` tool (sub-agent spawn) — does that interact with crews?

6. **Codex bash / shell tool semantics**: does codex have an async-bash mode analog to Claude's `run_in_background: true` and Copilot's `mode: "async"`? If not, how do we arm a long-running listener subprocess from inside a codex turn?

7. **Codex transcript format**: what does the events.jsonl analog look like? Is there a `tool.execution_start` / `system.notification` analog the bg-gate detector can scan? Or do we need a codex-specific bg-detection signal source (per the crews AGENTS.md v3.1.0 detector-extension guidance)?

8. **3-way env tiebreak**: extend `readSessionEnv()` to handle CODEX session id env vars (whatever they are — `CODEX_SESSION_ID`? `CODEX_AGENT_SESSION_ID`?). Tiebreak when all 3 are set.

9. **Launcher env scrub**: existing scrubs (Copilot launcher removes Claude session env, Claude launcher removes Copilot session env) need a 3-way variant: codex launcher removes Claude + Copilot session env.

10. **`.codex-plugin/` overlay scope**: do we ship 21 codex-flavored SKILL.md files? Or does codex's plugin model use a different discovery surface (e.g., agent-registry config)? Are the per-skill `<plugin>:<command>` colon mirrors needed?

11. **Copilot port lessons that DON'T apply**: Copilot port specifically dealt with Copilot's `ask_user` snake_case (v1.3.12) and Copilot's per-intent OSC title rewriter (v1.8.12) and Copilot's `wt.exe` interactions. Codex likely has its own pile of analogous engine-specific gotchas.

12. **Tab title**: codex displays its agent name where? wt.exe tab title? Console window title? Both? Does codex have an env var to disable per-turn title rewriting (analog to `COPILOT_DISABLE_TERMINAL_TITLE`)?

command.name: crews-redundant-empty-kind-tag-emissions
command.descriptionHtml: Brainstorm-first. Members emit redundant kind=done/progress envelopes with near-identical or empty bodies when their listener wakes without new substantive work. Observed on 2 independent machines/sessions. Documented as known v2-deferred per architecture-refactor.md option D, but v1.x mitigations (lead-side dedup, source-side suppression, wake-up filter, member kind-tag exemption) are likely feasible. Brainstorm to pick which mitigation.

prompts.brainstorm:
/brainstorm-with-ralph crews-redundant-empty-kind-tag-emissions

Context:

Observed on TWO independent machines + sessions:

1. **codexu v5.50 impl member (our session, 2026-06-04)**: `impl-worktree-conditional-narrow` sent seq 1 + seq 2 with IDENTICAL `kind=done` bodies (10 commits on ralph/.../tip 5bff9938; 9/9 stories pass; ...) and seq 3 = `kind=progress` with body "Listener crashed on mailbox lock contention. Re-arming. Listener re-armed. Impl is complete. Awaiting any lead follow-up via the mailbox. Idle." Three envelopes; one substantive.

2. **operator-reported other-PC session (seval-540475 crew, 2026-06-04)**: `summarizer-behavior` member sent 3 duplicate ack envelopes — all just status pings with no new substantive content. Lead's analysis attributed it to: listener wake-ups (from lead arm calls, fs.watch events, nag deliveries) force new turns; members must emit kind tag every turn (v1.8.1 lead exemption does NOT extend to members); with nothing substantive to say, member emits minimal `done` or `progress` stubs like "Listener re-armed" or "Listener already active".

Reportedly documented as a known design quirk: `plugins/crews/docs/architecture-refactor.md` option D ("side-channel listener queue") flagged it as a deferred 2.0 redesign of the "listener-exit-as-wakeup → new turn → required kind footer" model. Worth verifying this reference matches the canonical refactor doc before scoping mitigation work.

Why it matters:

- **Lead-side noise**: every redundant envelope creates a mailbox entry the lead has to consume + acknowledge via the STRICT-ACK contract. The dedup work goes to whoever's reviewing (operator or bookkeeper agent).
- **Compounding effect**: every consumed entry advances the cursor; the lead's `review-mail` has to scroll through more rows to find the substantive ones. With many members, this noise dominates the lead's mailbox.
- **Listener-arm pressure**: as a side effect of needing to ack the noise, the lead burns extra turns on review-mail + ack tags. The listener arm churn (from earlier sessions where re-arms happened every empty timeout cycle) was an analogous waste; the lead-protected `Don't re-arm on every empty timeout cycle` rule from codexu AGENTS.md (codified 2026-06-03) is the parallel discipline.

v1.x mitigation candidates the brainstorm should evaluate:

1. **Lead-side dedup on review-mail**: when 2+ consecutive consumed entries from the same sender have identical or near-identical bodies (within a configurable similarity threshold), collapse them into one displayed row with `count=N`. Cursor advances past all of them as if reviewed individually. Surface: `hooks/commands/review-mail.js::formatReviewMailEntry` + a new collapse pass. Tradeoff: silent collapse hides genuine duplicate emissions that might indicate a runaway loop; pair with a stderr warning when collapsing > 5 in a single batch.

2. **Source-side suppression**: member's Stop hook detects "would emit kind=done with body identical (or near-identical) to last emitted kind=done" and downgrades to no-op (skip outbox + skip mailbox-history write). Body comparison via hash. Surface: `hooks/stop.js` near the report-tag write site. Tradeoff: re-introduces the "silent-censor" failure mode the v1.4.x crews team explicitly fixed; needs a tight similarity threshold + a stderr warning.

3. **Listener wake-up filter**: ignore fs.watch events that don't correspond to actual inbox additions (delete events, attr-only changes, parent-dir touches). Today the listener wakes on ANY change to the watched dir. Surface: `lib/listener-loop.js` watch handler. Tradeoff: complexity (correlate fs.watch events vs. inbox-line additions); may not catch all wake-up sources (arm calls, heartbeat side-effects).

4. **Member kind-tag exemption when wake was spurious**: when the listener wakes the member but the inbox queue is unchanged since the last turn, exempt the member's next turn from the kind-tag requirement (v1.8.1 lead exemption pattern, extended to members under specific conditions). Surface: `hooks/stop.js::shouldRequireKindTag`. Tradeoff: weakens the kind-tag invariant that's load-bearing for proactive-routing.

5. **Architectural-refactor option D (full v2)**: side-channel listener queue separating wake-ups from turn-emission. Out of scope for v1.x; track separately if the brainstorm thinks v1.x mitigations are insufficient.

6. **Status-quo accept**: do nothing; tolerate the noise; let the bookkeeper learn to skip identical-body rows visually. Cost: ongoing UX friction; benefit: zero implementation risk.

Gaps the brainstorm should investigate:

- **Verify the architecture-refactor.md option D reference**: read `plugins/crews/docs/architecture-refactor.md` and confirm option D actually describes this issue + what its v2 plan is. The other-machine analysis cited it but we should ground-truth.
- **Identify the spurious wake-up source(s)**: when does the listener actually wake without a real new mailbox entry? Profile via crews.log under stress, or instrument `listener-loop.js` watch handler.
- **Quantify the noise**: in a typical multi-member session, what fraction of envelopes are substantive vs. status pings? Pull from a recent session's `mailbox-history.jsonl`.
- **Cross-check with v1.8.1 lead exemption**: that fix solved exactly the analogous lead-side problem; what's the structural reason members weren't exempted at the same time?
- **Cross-check with v3.4 lead-listener-unconditional**: it formalized the lead's listener-always-armed rule; does v3.4 + this redundant-emit pattern compound (lead wakes lead, lead arms, lead's arm wakes member, member emits stub)?

Deliverable:

Multi-lens brainstorm (Codex feasibility + Copilot product-reality + Devil's advocate + Claude synthesis) → `selected-direction.md` ready for `/plan-with-ralph --from-brainstorm`. The synthesized direction should:

- Pick the ONE v1.x mitigation to ship first (with a clear ordering rationale).
- Identify the surface size + risk for each candidate (some are 50-line plugin changes, some require new tests).
- Explicitly defer (or NOT defer) the v2 option-D architectural redesign — if the v1.x mitigations are sufficient, the v2 work may not be needed.
- Identify any side effects on the existing review-required gate (v1.2.9), STRICT-ACK contract (v1.1.5), and proactive-routing (v1.2.11+).
- Identify ANY test coverage gaps — this issue happens at the intersection of listener-loop, fs.watch, Stop hook, kind-tag invariant, and mailbox writes; tests likely need to span multiple files.

DO NOT ship a mitigation that silently censors substantive content. Every suppression path needs (a) a stderr warning when activated, (b) an env-var off switch (e.g., CREWS_DEDUP_KIND_EMITS=off), (c) telemetry to crews.log so operators can grep for false suppressions.

/plan-with-ralph "Schema cleanup — consolidate 5 inter-related changes to the OverviewTask + RalphPipelineState + CrewSessionRef schemas. All touch types.ts; doing them as one PR per repo avoids deprecation-alias churn from sequential changes.

The hand-curated bookkeeper field collides with the watcher-derived RalphStage enum (both have 'plan-ready' + 'shipped' values, different meanings). Decouple:

- Field: phase → lifecycle (in OverviewTask interface).
- Values: plan-ready → tracked, shipped → merged, closed → archived.

## Change B — Restructure command.planPrompt → command.prompts

The singular planPrompt field has been overloaded with /brainstorm-with-ralph and /plan-with-ralph and /implement-with-ralph content. Rename + restructure:

- `command.planPrompt: string` → `command.prompts: { brainstorm?: string, plan?: string, impl?: string }`.
- Bookkeeper authors whichever phase(s) are anticipated starting points.
- Supports REGRESSIONS: if a planner finds a gap and the task regresses to brainstorming, the stored prompts.brainstorm is reused for the new brainstorm member.
- Maintain back-compat alias: if `command.prompts` is absent, fall back to reading `command.planPrompt` as `prompts.plan`. Drop the alias one minor later.

## Change C — Add OverviewTask.initialStage?: RalphStage

The bookkeeper's intent for where the task should kick off. Optional; auto-defaulted when absent:
- prompts.brainstorm set + no prompts.plan → initialStage='brainstorming'
- prompts.plan set → initialStage='planning'
- prompts.impl set + no prompts.plan → initialStage='plan-ready' (rare; only when plan.md lives externally)

The runtime deriveNextCommand uses initialStage as the starting-point hint when no .ralph/<dirs>/ filesystem state exists yet.

## Change D — Add phase field to CrewSessionRef

Derived from memberName prefix (brainstorm-* / plan-* / impl-*). Decouples 'phase the member intended to run' from 'stage the task was in when discovered.' Documented in detail in the prior .ralph-overview/data.json entry for ralph-overview-crew-session-phase-field (now consolidated into this task).

- Each regression spawns a FRESH crew member of the regressed phase (per feedback_phase_discipline_separate_members). The new member reads the relevant prompts.<phase> seed from .ralph-overview/data.json.

Verify zero residual 'phase:' or top-level 'planPrompt:' occurrences after.

command.name: crews-roles-and-direct-operator-channel
command.descriptionHtml: Brainstorm-first. Redesign crews plugin roles to formalize a 3-party model: user (human operator) ↔ lead ↔ members. Today the plugin only models lead↔member; the human is an implicit out-of-band actor with no plugin awareness. Outcomes wanted: (1) explicit role title for the human (e.g. operator) so leads + members can refer to them consistently in prose; (2) explicit role title for the lead (e.g. lead — likely formalize existing usage); (3) define when the lead should escalate to user-direct-member interaction; (4) define how the user notifies the lead about an out-of-band interaction they just had with a member; (5) ideally surface user↔member direct chats in the lead's mail/history trail automatically (mirroring how progress envelopes flow) so the lead doesn't lose context.

warnings.html: ⚠️ Multiple competing approaches on each axis: naming (operator/principal/owner/director/human; lead/orchestrator/coordinator/scrum-master/PM), direct-channel mechanism (auto-detect via member's mailbox event-stream / explicit user CLI command / magic-prefix in member terminal / mailbox notification on next session-resume / nothing — trust transcripts), and lead-side surface (separate inbox category / merged into review-mail / dashboard-only / silent until lead asks). Brainstorm should pressure-test each. Touches plugin manifest schema (new actor role), hooks (SessionStart/PostToolUse/Stop), CLI commands, and operator-facing docs in BOTH crews CLAUDE.md and per-engine briefings. Affects every existing crew lead's mental model — coordinate with the in-flight overview-bookkeeper session before rolling out.

prompts.brainstorm:
/brainstorm-with-ralph "Redesign the crews plugin to formalize a 3-party actor model (user ↔ lead ↔ members) with named roles and a defined user-to-member direct-interaction channel.

## Why this matters

Today the crews plugin coordinates 2 parties: leads and members. The human operating the workspace is OUTSIDE the plugin's model — leads relay messages to/from 'the operator' as untyped prose, members never address them directly, and the plugin's hooks/CLI commands have no concept of the human's identity or interaction surface.

This works for the common case but breaks down when:
- A lead's session output addresses 'the operator' generically — members who read shared threads see 'lead said: ask operator about X' but have no canonical way to refer back.
- The human wants to go DIRECTLY to a member's terminal and interact (debug something interactively, demo a UI, type a quick correction). Today this happens out-of-band: the lead never sees the interaction, the member has to ad-hoc explain it later.
- The lead should sometimes ASK the human to take a direct action on a member (e.g. 'the member needs to see your screen' or 'this is a 5-message debugging dance, just go to their terminal'). Today there's no protocol — the lead types prose hoping the human reads it.
- The human has interacted with the member directly and now wants the lead to know what happened. Today they have to manually re-explain to the lead.

## Design axes the brainstorm must pressure-test

### Axis 1 — Naming

For the LEAD's role: keep `lead` (matches existing plugin terminology) vs rename to `orchestrator` / `coordinator` / `scrum-master` / `PM`. `lead` is in active use; rename would be churn unless brainstorm finds a strong reason.

For the USER's role: `operator` (matches my bookkeeper docs) vs `principal` (auth-like) vs `owner` (overloaded) vs `director` vs `human` (too generic). Brainstorm should propose the term that least conflicts with existing plugin / Claude Code / Copilot vocabulary AND is natural in prose ('operator paused the job', 'operator confirmed the merge').

### Axis 2 — Direct user↔member channel mechanism

When the human goes to a member's terminal and types directly, how does the plugin detect + log it?

A. **Nothing.** Trust transcripts. Lead reads member's lastTurnAt + transcriptPath if curious.
B. **Auto-detect via stdin source.** Plugin hooks (PreToolUse / new) flag a turn whose first user message was typed locally (vs delivered via mailbox). Tag the manifest/mailbox-history entry with `via: 'operator-direct'`.
C. **Explicit CLI command.** User runs `crews.js operator-message <member-name> --crew <crew> <text>` from any terminal; plugin posts as an `operator-direct` envelope into the member's inbox AND into the lead's review queue.
D. **Magic prefix in member terminal.** User types `OPERATOR:` or similar as the first line; member's PostToolUse parses and emits an `operator-direct` log entry.
E. **Hybrid.** B + C, with manifest field `lastOperatorDirectAt` derived from whichever fires.

Lens against: latency (how fast does lead know), false-positive risk (B might mis-flag), discoverability (D needs user to remember the prefix), maintenance burden.

### Axis 3 — When should the lead ASK the user to do direct interaction?

Formalize the escalation pattern with named triggers:

- **interactive-debug-needed:** member is in a 3+ turn interactive debugging loop where the lead-relay overhead would dominate.
- **demo-required:** the member needs to show a UI/build/output the human must visually inspect.
- **paused-on-real-time-question:** member's kind=question requires sub-30s response cycle.
- **transcript-too-large-to-relay:** member's context is huge and the lead can't summarize fast enough.

Provide a slash command or envelope kind (e.g. `kind=escalate-to-operator`) that leads emit to BOTH the operator AND the member, signaling 'go talk directly'.

### Axis 4 — How the user notifies the lead about a direct interaction

After the user has gone direct, how do they tell the lead 'I just did X with member Y'?

P. **CLI command:** `crews.js notify-lead --crew <crew> --about <member> <summary>` posts an envelope into the lead's review queue tagged `kind=operator-direct-summary`.
Q. **Member auto-summary on next turn:** the member detects the operator-direct turn(s) just happened, summarizes in its next kind=progress envelope so the lead's normal mail-review surface picks it up.
R. **Lead dashboard recomputes from manifest:** lead's `list-members` command shows a per-member 'lastOperatorDirectAt' column; lead reads transcript on demand.
S. **Silent until lead reviews member transcript:** simplest; least proactive.

### Axis 5 — Lead-side surface

Where/how does the lead see operator-direct events?

- Separate review-mail category (`/crews:review-operator-direct`)
- Merged into existing review-mail with a visual flag
- Dashboard-only (list-members column)
- Both inbox + dashboard
- None — lead asks explicitly

## Constraints / non-negotiable invariants

1. Backwards compatible: existing leads + members without role-aware code keep working. New role surfaces are additive.
2. Cross-engine: claude-code AND copilot hooks need the same surface (per the recent migration audit's lessons).
3. Don't break the v1.6.2 listener-arm gate or v1.7.x sessionId pointer index.
4. Bookkeeper-lead (overview-bookkeeper) should NOT need to change its operating model dramatically — this is additive UX, not a rewrite.
5. Operator notify-CLI commands must work without requiring the operator to know which crew/lead they belong to (auto-discover from cwd, similar to crews.js's existing cwd-discovery patterns).

## Reference + investigation

- Current plugin manifest at `./ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/crews/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` + same path under `.copilot-plugin/`.
- Hooks at `plugins/crews/hooks/{SessionStart,stop,pre-tool-use,post-tool-use}.js` (+ Copilot mirrors). These are where role-aware logic would live.
- CLI at `plugins/crews/tools/crews.js` — would gain `operator-message`, `notify-lead`, or whatever the brainstorm chooses.
- Mailbox envelope schema at `plugins/crews/hooks/lib/mailbox.js` (or wherever envelope kinds are defined) — would gain new kinds.
- Existing `actor` concept in manifests — review whether adding a 3rd actor role (operator) makes sense or whether operator is fundamentally different (no manifest, no listener, but has identity).
- Auto-memory `feedback_check_mailbox_after_tool_bursts` documents one ad-hoc operator-interaction pattern.

Lenses: feasibility (codex — what's the plumbing actually look like?), product-reality (copilot — would real operators use the CLI?), devil's-advocate (does formalizing this just add overhead operators won't bother with?), simplification (lightest mechanism that captures 80% of the value).

## Deliverable

At end of brainstorm Phase 5, produce `.ralph/brainstorms/crews-roles-and-direct-operator-channel/selected-direction.md` with:

- Recommended naming (lead-role term + operator-role term) with rationale.
- Recommended direct-channel mechanism (A-E or hybrid) with rationale.
- Recommended lead-side surface (separate category / merged / dashboard / etc).
- Concrete escalation triggers (named, with examples) and the slash command / envelope-kind to fire them.
- Concrete user-to-lead notify mechanism (P-S or hybrid).
- Migration story: how existing crews v1.7.x sessions absorb the new model.
- Acceptance criteria for eventual impl.
- Open questions for the planner.

Do NOT chain into /plan-with-ralph. The bookkeeper spawns a fresh plan-crews-roles-and-direct-operator-channel member from the selected-direction.md per phase discipline."

prompts.plan:
/plan-with-ralph "Migrate ralph-overview data layout to .ralph-overview/ with JSON-only source-of-truth + a generated/ subdir for all watcher output.

## Design is LOCKED (do not re-litigate — plan around these)

Final target layout (codexu reference; plugin defaults should match):

```
.ralph-overview/
├── config.json                 ← hand-curated config (was .ralph-overview/config.json)
├── data.json                   ← hand-curated source (was .ralph-overview/data.json)
├── SCHEMA.md                   ← extracted from the leading comment block of .ralph-overview/data.json
└── generated/                  ← TRACKED in git, watcher writes exclusively here
    ├── snapshot.json
    ├── ralph-state.json
    ├── recommendations.json
    ├── dependency-graph.json
    ├── activity.jsonl
    ├── snapshot.schema.json
    ├── overview.html           ← viewer build artifact
    └── .lock/
        ├── sync.lock           ← was .ralph/overview-sync.lock
        └── watcher.owner       ← was .ralph/overview-watcher.owner
```

Locked decisions from the operator (don't re-debate):
1. **Track `generated/` in git** — fresh clones / CI / agents get usable state without running the watcher first. Matches today's behavior (the current `plans/overview-*.json` files are tracked).
2. **Drop the `overview-` prefix inside `generated/`** — the parent dir name already conveys the context.
3. **`overview.html` lives at `.ralph-overview/generated/overview.html`** — sibling to the data sidecars, not under a separate `viewer/` subdir.
4. **Lock files live at `.ralph-overview/generated/.lock/*`** — even though they're runtime coordination markers (not data), this keeps everything-state-related under one top-level subdir.
5. **Pure JSON, not JSONC** — the schema doc currently atop `.ralph-overview/data.json` extracts to a sibling `SCHEMA.md` rather than living as `//` comments inside the data file. Pure JSON parses everywhere without parser-choice ceremony.

## Cross-repo scope — plan must address both

### Repo A — `D:/ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/ralph-overview/` (the plugin)

Must ship FIRST as a minor-version bump (suggested: v2.x — confirm against the plugin's existing version trajectory and CHANGELOG). Plugin changes:

- **P1. Data loader accepts JSON.** `scripts/lib/parse-overview-data.mjs` currently uses `@babel/parser` and requires exactly 1 top-level statement (rejecting codexu's `globalThis.window = …` polyfill + `window.OVERVIEW_DATA = …` two-statement shape). Replace with: auto-detect by extension. For `.json`, use plain `JSON.parse`; for `.js`, keep the existing AST path for back-compat. Side-effect: fixes the pre-existing 1-statement strictness bug that currently blocks `pnpm sync-ralph-state` on codexu HEAD.
- **P2. Viewer reads JSON via fetch bootstrap.** `tools/overview-viewer/` currently relies on `<script src=".ralph-overview/data.json">` setting `window.OVERVIEW_DATA` + `window.OVERVIEW_RALPH_STATE` before React mounts. Replace with a small async bootstrap that `fetch()`-es the JSON files and populates the globals (or React state) before the tree renders. Preserve all current render behavior; suspense-style loading state is acceptable.
- **P3. Plugin skills become MCP-only or config-aware.** `skills/{work-on,triage,blocker-report}/SKILL.md` and the matching `.copilot-plugin/copilot-skills/*` Copilot mirrors currently reference `.ralph-overview/generated/snapshot.json` literally. Decision the plan must make: do skills (a) call MCP tools exclusively and never touch files, or (b) resolve `outputs.snapshot` from `overview-config.json` first. Operator prefers (a) — MCP becomes the single read interface — but if MCP doesn't expose everything skills need, mixed-mode is acceptable for v1 with full MCP-only as a follow-up. Either way, NO hardcoded file paths in skill bodies after this lands.
- **P4. Writer + default-config emit the new layout.** `scripts/lib/default-config.mjs` changes defaults from `plans/*` to `.ralph-overview/generated/*` with the prefix-stripped basenames. `dataFile` default becomes `.ralph-overview/data.json`. Honor existing `outputs.*` overrides in user `overview-config.json` for back-compat with old-layout consumers.
- **P5. Lock-path resolution.** Wherever the watcher currently composes `<repoRoot>/.ralph/overview-sync.lock` and `<repoRoot>/.ralph/overview-watcher.owner` (search the plugin codebase — likely in `scripts/lib/sync-core.mjs` and `WatcherSupervisor` for the MCP side), change defaults to `<repoRoot>/.ralph-overview/generated/.lock/sync.lock` and `…/watcher.owner`. Lock creation must mkdir-p the `.lock/` path on first use. Honor existing `lockFile` config override for back-compat.
- **P6. Tests.** Add tests for: JSON loader path; viewer bootstrap fetches and populates state correctly; default config writes to new locations; lock-path mkdir-p behavior; back-compat with old `outputs.*` overrides. Update any test that asserts `.ralph-overview/generated/snapshot.json` to the new default.
- **P7. CHANGELOG entry.** Document the migration, the back-compat story, the deprecation timeline (if any) for the legacy `.js` loader and `plans/` defaults.

### Repo B — `D:/harness-efforts/codexu/` (this repo)

Adopts the plugin's new defaults AFTER the plugin ships. Codexu changes:

- **C1. Convert data file.** Strip the leading 19-line schema-doc comment + the `globalThis.window = …` polyfill + the `window.OVERVIEW_DATA =` assignment from `.ralph-overview/data.json`. Write the object literal as pure JSON to `.ralph-overview/data.json`. Move the comment block to `.ralph-overview/SCHEMA.md` (preserve all schema notes; format as proper markdown).
- **C2. Move + rewrite config.** `.ralph-overview/config.json` → `.ralph-overview/config.json`. Update every `outputs.*` path to `.ralph-overview/generated/<prefix-stripped>.json`. Set `dataFile` to `.ralph-overview/data.json`. Update `lockFile` to `.ralph-overview/generated/.lock/sync.lock` (or just drop the override and inherit the plugin's new default).
- **C3. Delete stale files.** After `pnpm sync-ralph-state` confirms the new layout is being regenerated correctly: `git rm` the legacy `.ralph-overview/data.json`, `.ralph-overview/generated/snapshot.json`, `.ralph-overview/generated/ralph-state.{js,json}`, `plans/overview-recommendations.json`, `plans/overview-dependency-graph.json`, `plans/overview-activity.jsonl`, `.ralph-overview/generated/snapshot.schema.json`, `plans/overview.html`, `plans/overview.html.next`, and the watcher-related entries in `.ralph/`. Keep design-doc markdowns in `plans/` (overview-data-split.md, overview-viewer-polish-seed.md, overview-vite-react.md — these are human-written context).
- **C4. Update `package.json` script paths.** The `overview`, `sync-ralph-state`, etc. scripts call into the plugin via `bin/ralph-overview.mjs` (the gitignored resolver wrapper). The wrapper itself doesn't need changes for this migration — it dispatches to the plugin's `bin/ralph-overview.mjs` which gets the new layout via the plugin update. But VERIFY the wrapper still resolves correctly after the plugin version bump.
- **C5. Docs.** Update every reference to the old paths in AGENTS.md (multiple), `docs/fork-roadmap.md` if any, `docs/fork-notes.md` if any, `plans/overview-data-split.md`, plus the recent 'Copilot migration milestone' block (which mentions the `parseOverviewData` 1-statement bug — that bug will be FIXED by P1; update the block to reflect that). Find-and-replace `.ralph-overview/generated/snapshot.json` → `.ralph-overview/generated/snapshot.json`, etc.
- **C6. Smoke-verify end-to-end.** After plugin install: run `pnpm sync-ralph-state` (must succeed and write to new locations), `pnpm overview` (must serve the viewer with data populated), `mcp__ralph-overview__overview_parallel_ready_tasks` (must return non-empty results from the new snapshot location).

## Sequencing constraint

Plugin (Repo A) MUST ship its minor-version bump BEFORE codexu (Repo B) adopts. During the window between plugin-ship and codexu-adopt, codexu's `pnpm sync-ralph-state` continues to work because the plugin still honors `outputs.*` overrides in the existing `.ralph-overview/config.json`. Plan must explicitly call this out so the impl member doesn't try to land both changes in one cross-repo PR.

## Open questions the plan must resolve (not the operator's job — answer in the plan)

1. Plugin version-bump magnitude: minor (v2.x with `dataFile` default change) or major (v3.0.0 if any consumer reads the .js form directly)?
2. Back-compat for `parseOverviewData('.ralph-overview/data.json')`: keep the AST path with a `console.warn` deprecation for N minor versions, or hard-cut at the bump? Operator preference: keep one minor version with deprecation, then drop.
3. MCP-only skills vs config-aware skills (P3 above) — pick one, justify, list any new MCP tools needed if MCP-only.
4. Viewer bootstrap pattern: pre-React `await fetch + window.X = …` shim vs React-side `Suspense` + `useSWR`/`useEffect` fetch. Either is fine; pick by simplicity.
5. Should the lock-files subdir be `.lock/` (operator-specified) or something else more conventional like `.locks/` plural? Operator picked `.lock/` so default to that unless plan finds a strong reason to deviate.
6. Should codexu's `bin/ralph-overview.mjs` resolver wrapper be retired in favor of direct `node $CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT/...` or `node ${COPILOT_HOME}/installed-plugins/...` paths in `package.json` scripts? Probably out of scope for this migration — track as a follow-up.

## Reference — existing artifacts to read before planning

- `D:/harness-efforts/codexu/.ralph-overview/data.json` — the source we're migrating (~395KB, ~10K lines; mostly task entries).
- `D:/harness-efforts/codexu/.ralph-overview/config.json` — current config, every `outputs.*` field is here.
- `D:/ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/ralph-overview/scripts/lib/parse-overview-data.mjs` — the validator that currently rejects multi-statement JS.
- `D:/ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/ralph-overview/scripts/lib/default-config.mjs` (+ `.d.mts` + `resolve-config.mjs`) — where defaults live.
- `D:/ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/ralph-overview/tools/overview-viewer/` — React viewer.
- `D:/ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/ralph-overview/{skills,.copilot-plugin/copilot-skills}/{work-on,triage,blocker-report}/SKILL.md` — the 4 skill SKILL.md files (Claude + Copilot mirrors) hardcoding `.ralph-overview/generated/snapshot.json`.
- `D:/ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/ralph-overview/CHANGELOG.md` — recent entries for sense of version-bump magnitude conventions.
- `D:/harness-efforts/codexu/AGENTS.md` — the 'Copilot migration milestone' block references this task's parseOverviewData follow-up at item (b).

## Phase discipline + reporting

This is the PLAN phase (no brainstorm; design is locked above). Produce ONLY a plan deliverable (e.g. `.ralph/jobs/ralph-overview-data-relocation-and-json-migration/plan.md` and any stories/decomposition the plan-with-ralph skill generates). Do NOT chain into `/implement-with-ralph` — the bookkeeper will spawn a separate impl-phase member after FF'ing the plan to main.

COMMIT TARGET: lead is on `main`. Commit your plan on a fresh topic branch off main (`ralph/plan-ralph-overview-data-relocation-and-json-migration`), push to `origin`, and report commit SHA + branch in your kind=done body.

REPORTING (crews v1.8.x body-canonical hard-block): final turn ends with `<|report kind=\"done\" summary=\"<short>\"|>`. Substantive content (commit SHA, branch, plan summary, open questions, anomalies) in PROSE BODY. Summary > 200 chars + body < 50 chars triggers reject.

Note any Copilot engine anomalies (hook quirks, listener issues, CLI errors) in prose — this spawn is also a smoke-test data point for the v1.8.11 caller-engine default (you should have been spawned as a Copilot member without my passing --engine; verify your manifest engine field if you can."

command.name: codexu-bin-ralph-overview-wrapper-retirement
command.descriptionHtml: Plan-first. Retire codexu's gitignored bin/ralph-overview.mjs resolver wrapper. The wrapper is a legacy bootstrap that predates the ralph-overview plugin's modern scripts/init-consumer.mjs pattern (which emits package.json scripts that delegate directly to $CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT/ralph-overview/bin/ralph-overview.mjs). Because it's in .gitignore, any local-machine fix to it (e.g., the in-session 2026-05-29 Copilot-path addition) doesn't propagate to other clones. Options the plan must evaluate: (a) re-run overview-init to regenerate package.json in the modern direct-path form (works on Claude only — $CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT is unset on Copilot CLI); (b) un-ignore /bin/ and commit the wrapper with cross-engine support baked in; (c) push cross-engine awareness UPSTREAM to scripts/init-consumer.mjs so every consumer benefits without a per-consumer wrapper.

warnings.html: ⚠️ Cross-engine constraint. Copilot CLI does NOT export a $CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT or equivalent $COPILOT_PLUGIN_ROOT env var (verified against the official Copilot CLI plugin reference + hooks reference docs 2026-05-29). The plugin install lives at ~/.copilot/installed-plugins/ai-developer-toolkit/<plugin>/ (single live copy, no versioned subdir) but consumers have no built-in env var pointing there. Any retirement option must keep pnpm sync-ralph-state + pnpm overview working under BOTH engines without per-developer shell-profile setup. Recommend option (c) — push upstream — as the architecturally cleanest answer; option (b) is the fallback if upstream is too slow.

Copilot CLI does NOT export an equivalent var (verified against https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/copilot-cli-reference/cli-plugin-reference and https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/hooks-reference 2026-05-29 — Copilot only exports `COPILOT_AGENT_SESSION_ID`, `COPILOT_CLI`, `COPILOT_CLI_BINARY_VERSION`, `COPILOT_LOADER_PID`, `COPILOT_RUN_APP`, plus `COPILOT_HOME` for user-config override).

## Goal

`pnpm sync-ralph-state` and `pnpm overview` must work on BOTH engines (Claude Code + Copilot CLI) without:
- Per-developer shell-profile setup (`$RALPH_OVERVIEW_PLUGIN_ROOT` exported by every contributor's shell rc — operator burden too high)
- A per-consumer gitignored wrapper that drifts out of sync across machines
- Breaking existing Claude Code workflows that already use the direct `$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` path

## Three candidate paths (plan must pick + justify)

### Option A — re-run `overview-init` to regenerate `package.json` scripts in the plugin's modern direct-path form

Writes `"sync-ralph-state": "node $CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT/ralph-overview/bin/ralph-overview.mjs sync --repo ."`. Cleanest from the plugin's POV. **Blocker:** breaks under Copilot CLI (no `$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT`). Would need a parallel Copilot-friendly variant (perhaps a `npm run` cross-shell prelude). Not viable as-is.

### Option B — un-ignore `/bin/` and commit the wrapper with cross-engine support

Local-to-codexu, ships today. Removes the gitignore entry on `/bin/`, commits the existing wrapper with its current cross-engine cascade (Claude install paths + the new Copilot install path I added in-session). Every machine clones a working wrapper. **Downside:** doesn't help OTHER consumers of the ralph-overview plugin who may hit the same Copilot-path gap. Pragmatic short-term fix; doesn't address the root cause.

### Option C — push cross-engine awareness UPSTREAM into `scripts/init-consumer.mjs`

Update the plugin's init flow to emit `package.json` scripts that work on BOTH engines. Three sub-strategies:

   C1. Emit a TINY consumer-side wrapper at install time (essentially what codexu has, but generated + tracked by the plugin's init). Every consumer that runs `overview-init` gets a cross-engine wrapper checked in.
   C2. Emit `package.json` scripts using a cross-shell helper (e.g. `node -e 'import(...).then(...)'` that resolves the plugin path at runtime). Ugly but no wrapper file needed.
   C3. Emit `package.json` scripts that branch on env: `"sync-ralph-state": "node ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT:-${COPILOT_HOME:-$HOME/.copilot}/installed-plugins/ai-developer-toolkit}/ralph-overview/bin/ralph-overview.mjs sync --repo ."`. Bash expansion works on Unix; PowerShell-only Windows users break. Need cross-shell.

Option C is the right architectural answer (helps every consumer) but takes longer (plugin v-bump + adoption cycle).

## Plan must specify

1. **Pick A/B/C** (or hybrid) with clear rationale.
2. **If C:** which sub-strategy (C1/C2/C3) and why; what plugin tests need adding.
3. **Migration story:** if changing the wrapper's location or `package.json` script form, how do existing dev clones absorb the change cleanly (delete old wrapper, regenerate, etc.)?
4. **Cross-engine smoke test:** how to verify `pnpm sync-ralph-state` works under both Claude Code and Copilot CLI before merging. Manual test plan acceptable.
5. **Upstream-feature-request follow-up (Option D, parallel track):** draft a feature request to the GitHub Copilot CLI team proposing a `COPILOT_PLUGIN_ROOT_<KEBAB-PLUGIN-NAME>` env var or `copilot plugin path <name>` subcommand for parity with Claude Code. Not blocking this task, but a long-term cleaner solution if upstream lands it. The plan should include the draft text.
