command.name: crews-stop-member-hard-terminate-no-envelope
command.descriptionHtml: Plan-first. Today's stop-member is a SOFT authorization: it sets shutdownRequested=true + appends a stop-request envelope to the member's mailbox, then waits for the member's next turn to read the request and emit a kind=done ack. This costs ONE extra model invocation per member shutdown (the ack turn does no useful work — just says 'ok, dying') and generates a spurious second kind=done envelope that the lead must review. For the common case — bookkeeper wants a member gone because its task is complete — this round-trip is pure overhead. The operator's intent (2026-05-29): when a member is no longer needed, the lead should HARD-TERMINATE the launcher process + wt.exe tab, NOT send a polite stop-request envelope. Plan must design: (1) hard-terminate mechanism (Stop-Process on launcher PID + identify-and-kill the wt.exe tab); (2) API shape (new kill-member subcommand vs --hard flag on existing stop-member vs flipping the default and adding --soft for the ack-flow); (3) manifest state changes (listenerState, actorState, audit-log entry); (4) cross-platform behavior (Windows wt.exe vs Mac/Linux terminal-emulator equivalents); (5) edge cases (launcher PID already dead, wt.exe tab already closed, child Copilot CLI session not under launcher's process tree).

warnings.html: ⚠️ CRITICAL: do NOT kill the wt.exe server process. The wt.exe server hosts ALL tabs in a Windows Terminal window (and possibly across windows) — killing it would close every tab including unrelated crews members, the bookkeeper-lead's own session, and any dev shells the operator has open. The CORRECT mechanism is to kill ONLY the per-member child process inside the spawned tab AND explicitly close the tab. Empirical 2026-05-29: killing just the child process (Copilot CLI / PowerShell host) leaves the tab open as a 'process exited' placeholder — that's UNACCEPTABLE. The plan MUST combine TWO steps: (1) kill the per-tab child process tree (Copilot CLI + parent PowerShell, walking DOWN from Copilot CLI's PID; STOP at the boundary going UP — never include wt.exe server in the kill set); (2) explicitly close the tab via wt.exe --window <wid> close-tab --tabid <tid> or equivalent CLI subcommand (verify against Windows Terminal docs). Requires capturing the wt window ID + tab ID at spawn time (currently NOT in the manifest — needs to be added). DO NOT rely on the user's closeOnExit profile setting being graceful — empirical evidence shows tabs persist as placeholders, suggesting the user's setting may be automatic or never. Process-tree topology: the crews launcher is a PowerShell script (launcherPid in the manifest). It spawns wt.exe new-tab, which delegates to the long-running wt.exe server — the new tab is NOT a child of the launcher script. Touches: hooks/actors.js::spawnMember (capture per-member child PIDs + wt window/tab ID at spawn), hooks/commands/stop-member.js (new hard-terminate path that kills the child tree AND closes the tab, NEVER targeting the wt.exe server), tools/stop-member.js (CLI mirror), tests with explicit assertions on (a) wt.exe server PID survives, AND (b) the spawned tab is no longer present in wt -w <wid> list-tabs output.

prompts.plan:
/plan-with-ralph "Add hard-terminate capability to crews stop-member so the lead can kill a no-longer-needed member's per-tab child process WITHOUT killing the wt.exe server (which would close all sibling tabs) and WITHOUT the soft ack-and-shutdown round-trip via stop-request envelope.

## Why

The current `stop-member` (in `D:/ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/crews/hooks/commands/stop-member.js` and CLI mirror `tools/stop-member.js`) is a soft authorization:

1. Sets `manifest.shutdownRequested = true` and `manifest.listenerState = exited`
2. Appends a `stop-request` envelope to the member's mailbox
3. The member's next turn reads the stop-request, emits a `kind=done` ack turn
4. Member's Stop hook permits the turn to end; Copilot/Claude session may then exit

Observed cost (2026-05-29 smoke-test, validated): for every clean stop, the bookkeeper-lead receives TWO `kind=done` envelopes from the same member — first the task-completion done, then the stop-acknowledgement done. The second one is pure overhead: no useful work, just 'ok, dying.' The lead must review it (mid-turn nag fires, listener re-arms, etc.) — burning lead-side model invocations too. For an autonomous bookkeeper running dozens of members per day, this is a real tax.

Operator intent: when a member is no longer needed (the common case after a kind=done task report), HARD-TERMINATE the per-member child process tree AND force the tab to visually close. No envelope, no ack round-trip, no second model invocation, no orphaned 'process exited' tab placeholder. **Empirical 2026-05-29: operator observed that in prior smoke-test runs, the tab persisted open with no PowerShell inside it after termination — an empty placeholder.** That's unacceptable; the plan's solution MUST make the tab actually disappear, independent of the user's `closeOnExit` profile setting. The wt.exe server (which hosts ALL tabs in the window) MUST survive untouched.

## Tab-closure acceptance criterion

**The wt tab must visually disappear after hard-terminate, not persist as a 'process exited' placeholder.** Killing the child process alone is not sufficient — empirical evidence shows tabs linger. The plan MUST design a deterministic close-the-tab mechanism. Candidate strategies (plan picks one + justifies):

   T1. **Explicit `wt.exe close-tab` call after kill.** `wt --window <wid> close-tab --tabid <tid>` (verify exact subcommand against Windows Terminal CLI docs). Requires capturing the wt window ID + tab ID at spawn time. Currently NOT in the manifest — needs to be added.
   T2. **Spawn into a dedicated 'crews-member' profile with `closeOnExit: graceful` baked in.** Modify user's wt settings.json at install time. Intrusive but works for all exits. 
   T3. **UI automation (Ctrl+Shift+W keystroke to the focused tab).** Hacky, fragile, last resort.
   T4. **Hybrid T1 + T2.** Most robust, most code.

   Operator leaning: **T1** if wt CLI supports tab-id-targeted close in the user's wt version; fall back to T4 if not. Plan must verify wt CLI capabilities empirically.

## CRITICAL CONSTRAINT — do NOT kill the wt.exe server

The wt.exe server is a long-running process that hosts ALL tabs in a Windows Terminal window. The bookkeeper-lead's own tab, any other crews members' tabs, the operator's dev shells — all share the same wt.exe server. **Killing wt.exe = closing every tab = catastrophic.**

The correct target is the per-tab child process tree:
- The launcher PowerShell script (PID in `manifest.launcherPid`) — may already be exited by the time we want to kill, since its job is to invoke `wt.exe new-tab '<command>'` and exit.
- The Copilot CLI process inside the spawned tab (NOT currently tracked in the manifest — would need to capture at spawn time, possibly via a post-spawn `Get-WmiObject Win32_Process | where CommandLine -match "--name <member-name>"` lookup since Copilot CLI is launched as a grand-child of the wt.exe server, not of our launcher).
- The PowerShell that hosts the Copilot CLI process inside the tab (Copilot CLI runs inside `pwsh` or `powershell` by default in a wt tab).

The plan must:
1. Capture per-member child process PIDs at spawn time (or shortly after) so we know what to kill later.
2. Define a kill strategy that targets ONLY those PIDs — never the wt.exe server PID.
3. Verify the wt.exe `closeOnExit` profile setting is `graceful` (the default) so the tab auto-closes when its child exits.
4. Add a regression test that asserts the wt.exe server PID SURVIVES a hard-terminate (spawn member, capture wt.exe server PID via parent-of-tab-process lookup, hard-terminate the member, assert wt.exe server PID is still alive).

## Design questions for the plan

### Q1. API shape — three reasonable options:

   A. **New `kill-member` subcommand.** Keeps `stop-member` semantics intact for back-compat. `kill-member <name> --crew <crew> [--reason <text>]` does the hard-terminate. Pro: clear semantic separation. Con: two commands for very similar intent.

   B. **`--hard` flag on existing `stop-member`.** Default = soft (current behavior). `stop-member <name> --crew <crew> --hard [--reason <text>]` does hard-terminate. Pro: discoverable. Con: easy to forget the flag and pay the round-trip cost; current bookkeeper habit is to default-call stop-member.

   C. **Flip the default + add `--soft` opt-in.** Default = hard-terminate. `stop-member <name> --crew <crew> [--soft] [--reason <text>]`. Pro: matches operator intent (hard is the common case). Con: breaking change for any consumer that depends on the ack-flow (does anyone?). Plan must investigate.

Plan should pick one and justify. Operator leaning: **C** (flip the default), with a brief deprecation window if there are real consumers of the soft flow.

### Q2. Hard-terminate mechanism — Windows specifics (tab-only, NOT wt.exe server)

Investigate (verify via experimentation):

   - Does `Stop-Process -Id <launcherPid>` even matter? Probably not — by the time hard-terminate runs, the launcher PowerShell has long since exited (its job was to invoke `wt.exe new-tab '...'` and return).
   - Does the manifest currently capture the Copilot CLI process PID inside the tab? Look at `hooks/actors.js::spawnMember` for any post-spawn PID capture. If NOT, plan must add capture — strategies:
      - Post-spawn `Get-WmiObject Win32_Process | where CommandLine -match "--name <safeName>"` lookup, retried with exponential backoff until Copilot CLI process appears (typically 5-15s after spawn).
      - Stamp a unique env var (e.g. `CREWS_MEMBER_PID_MARKER`) via the launcher's `wt.exe new-tab` command and have the spawned shell capture its own PID into the manifest on first turn.
      - Use `COPILOT_LOADER_PID` env var (verified present in this session) — but that's set INSIDE the Copilot CLI process, not accessible from outside.
   - Walk the process-tree parent chain: from the Copilot CLI PID, find its parent (PowerShell inside the tab). Kill PARENT to take down both. STOP walking before reaching the wt.exe server.
   - Use `Stop-Process -Id <pid>` (graceful) first, then `-Force` if process still alive after a timeout.
   - Verify the wt.exe `closeOnExit` setting: read `$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Packages\Microsoft.WindowsTerminal_*\LocalState\settings.json` for the default profile's `closeOnExit` value. If user has set `never`, the tab will linger empty after the child exits; that's a UX nit, not a correctness issue.

   Suggest an exploratory script (deliverable as part of P1 in the plan): spawn a test member with CREWS_NO_LAUNCH=0 (real wt.exe spawn), capture wt.exe server PID + member's launcher PID + Copilot CLI PID via WMI lookup, then try each kill strategy in isolation, observe what survives. The script's output becomes the empirical basis for the kill-strategy decision.

### Q3. Mac / Linux behavior

The current `spawnMember` is Windows-only (errors out on non-Windows with 'spawn-member currently requires Windows'). So Q2's wt.exe-specific design is fine for v1. But the plan should sketch what the equivalent would look like on Mac (Terminal.app via osascript) and Linux (gnome-terminal / xterm via DBus or terminal-emulator CLI) so the API shape doesn't paint us into a corner.

### Q4. Manifest state + audit log

What does the manifest look like after a hard-terminate?

   - `listenerState`: 'exited' (same as soft stop)
   - `actorState`: 'cleared'? Or keep 'active' until a separate `clear-member` runs? Operator's intent — hard-terminate means 'this member is GONE' — so 'cleared' makes sense.
   - `shutdownRequested`: true (signals 'lead authorized this')
   - New `terminatedAt` + `terminationKind: 'hard'` + `terminationReason: <reason>` fields for audit
   - New `terminatedPids: { launcher, copilotCli, hostShell }` for forensic record of what was killed and what survived (esp. wt.exe server PID)
   - Log entry in the manifest's audit history (if such exists)

If actorState flips to 'cleared' automatically on hard-terminate, then `clear-member` becomes redundant for hard-terminated members — the cleanup happens in one shot. The plan should consider whether to merge `kill-member` and `clear-member` into one command, or keep them separate (clear-member also archives mailbox-history; that's a different operation).

### Q5. Edge cases

   - Launcher PID already dead (expected — launcher exits after invoking wt.exe new-tab): no-op for the kill; still target the Copilot CLI child + update manifest state.
   - wt.exe tab already closed by operator (Ctrl+W or X): the Copilot CLI child is already gone; lookup returns no PID; treat as no-op + update manifest.
   - Copilot CLI process not yet discoverable (just-spawned member): retry the WMI lookup with backoff up to N seconds; if still not found, log + soft-fail (proceed with manifest update without actually killing — the process will exit on its own eventually).
   - Multiple PIDs under the same launcher (Copilot CLI may have forked its own children — e.g., Node language servers, child processes for shell tools): walk the process tree DOWN from Copilot CLI's PID and kill all descendants, but STOP at the boundary going UP (never include wt.exe server in the kill set).
   - Member has unreviewed outgoing mail (kind=done not yet consumed by lead): kill anyway. The lead can still read the outbox after the process is gone (outbox is on disk).
   - Member is currently mid-turn (active model invocation): kill anyway. Risk: leaves the model's response truncated, possibly mid-tool-call. Probably acceptable but plan should note the risk.
   - Multiple wt.exe SERVERS running (rare — happens if user has Windows Terminal Stable + Preview both installed). Plan: find the server that owns OUR tab by walking up from Copilot CLI PID; never target any wt.exe server even if multiple are present.

### Q6. AGENTS.md operating-manual update

The codexu AGENTS.md workflow diagram says:

```
lead: /crews:stop-member <name> (do NOT chain into the next phase)
```

If Q1 picks option C (flip default), this stays correct but its semantics change — the bookkeeper should know the new default is hard. If Q1 picks A or B, update the diagram to use the new command/flag. Either way, AGENTS.md needs a line clarifying 'stop-member is now hard by default' or pointing to the new command, AND a safety note: 'hard-terminate kills only the per-tab child process tree; the wt.exe server (and all other tabs) survive untouched.'

## Plan-level guidance

- This is a small-surface change but with non-trivial Windows-process-tree investigation. Allocate a story for the investigation/experimentation specifically.
- Tests: process-kill tests are hard to write portably. Suggest a `tests/stop-member-hard-terminate.test.js` that spawns a no-launch member (CREWS_NO_LAUNCH=1 skips wt.exe), simulates a child process via a sleep, kills it via the new code path, asserts manifest state + process death. Cross-platform skip if not Windows. ALSO a `tests/stop-member-hard-terminate-wt-server-survives.test.js` (Windows-only, optional in CI) that does a REAL wt.exe spawn, captures the wt.exe server PID, hard-terminates the member, and asserts the wt.exe server PID is still alive after the kill.
- Version bump: minor (v1.9.0) if API change; patch if pure flag addition.
- CHANGELOG: document the round-trip-cost rationale, the soft-stop deprecation timeline (if applicable), and the EXPLICIT safety guarantee that hard-terminate never touches the wt.exe server.

## Reference

- `D:/ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/crews/hooks/commands/stop-member.js` — current soft-stop implementation.
- `D:/ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/crews/tools/stop-member.js` — CLI mirror.
- `D:/ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/crews/hooks/actors.js` — `spawnMember` (captures launcherPid; will need to also capture per-tab child PIDs for hard-terminate).
- `D:/harness-efforts/codexu/AGENTS.md` workflow diagram + duty table — references `/crews:stop-member`.
- 2026-05-29 smoke-test seq-3 and seq-4 envelopes from `plan-ralph-overview-data-relocation-and-json-migration` — empirical evidence of the round-trip cost (two kind=done envelopes per task, second one is pure overhead).
- Windows Terminal settings: `$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Packages\Microsoft.WindowsTerminal_*\LocalState\settings.json` — confirm default profile `closeOnExit: graceful` (or document the dependency on this setting in the CHANGELOG).

## Phase discipline + reporting

This is the PLAN phase. Produce ONLY a plan deliverable (e.g. `.ralph/jobs/crews-stop-member-hard-terminate-no-envelope/plan.md` and any stories the plan-with-ralph skill generates). Do NOT chain into impl.

COMMIT TARGET: lead is on `main`. Commit your plan on a fresh topic branch off main (`ralph/plan-crews-stop-member-hard-terminate-no-envelope`), push to `origin`, and report commit SHA + branch in your kind=done body.

IMPORTANT: per AGENTS.md, the lead's primary working dir stays on `main`. If `plan-with-ralph` defaults to checking out its topic branch in the primary dir (observed 2026-05-29 with `plan-ralph-overview-data-relocation-and-json-migration` — the member switched my checkout out from under me), use a worktree instead: `git worktree add ../codexu-plan-crews-hard-terminate ralph/plan-crews-stop-member-hard-terminate-no-envelope` and do your branching + committing inside that worktree. Report worktree path in your kind=done body so the lead can clean it up after FF.

REPORTING (crews v1.8.x body-canonical hard-block): final turn ends with `<|report kind=\"done\" summary=\"<short>\"|>`. Substantive content (commit SHA, branch, picked API option + rationale, process-tree investigation findings, EXPLICIT confirmation that the kill strategy targets only the per-tab child tree (never the wt.exe server), open questions for impl, anomalies) in PROSE BODY."

command.name: crews-protocol-v2-per-report-outbox
command.descriptionHtml: Plan-first (design locked). Move the crews outbox protocol from one-envelope-per-turn to one-row-per-report JSONL, with terminal-gated batch delivery to the lead. Surfaced 2026-05-30 by a Copilot member's multi-tag turn (3 progress emits + 1 final done) where parseTurnTags's first-tag-wins logic silently dropped the terminal done tag, leaving the lead seeing only the first progress summary from ~18min earlier. Operator considered last-wins / terminal-preference / severity-ordered merge variants but picked the more invasive per-row-rows shape: each <|report ...|> tag writes its own outbox row; the lead's listener fires only when ≥1 terminal kind is present in the unread tail and delivers the whole batch in one shot. warnings.html: ⚠️ v2.0.0 protocol bump. Changes the on-disk outbox shape (envelope wrapper retired in favor of per-row JSONL rows); changes listener semantics (terminal-gated batch fire instead of any-new-row fire); touches Stop hook, listener loop, review-mail / read-member / peek-mailbox commands + CLI mirrors, body-canonical detection, force-response gates, mail-resolution credit, format-progress-tail (retired), and ~30+ test files that assume one-envelope-per-turn. prompts.plan:
/plan-with-ralph "Move the crews outbox protocol from one-envelope-per-turn to one-row-per-report JSONL, with terminal-gated batch delivery to the lead.

## Why

Empirically observed 2026-05-29 during smoke-test of impl-plan-with-ralph-auto-worktree: a Copilot member emitted multiple <|report kind=\"...\"|> tags in a single Stop-hook turn (3 progress emits followed by a final done emit). The current parseTurnTags (D:/ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/crews/hooks/mailbox.js:761) uses first-tag-wins semantics — it locks kind/summary/replyTo to the FIRST tag seen and ignores all subsequent tags. Result: the envelope was written with kind=\"progress\" and the FIRST progress summary, silently discarding the terminal kind=\"done\" with the actual ship report (commit SHAs, validation results, recommendations).

Several attribute-merging fixes were considered (last-wins, terminal-preference, severity-ordered, body-merge variants) but all introduce different edge cases. Operator picked a more invasive but cleaner shape: every <|report|> tag becomes its own outbox row, and consumption batches the trail when at least one terminal row is present.

## Locked design (do NOT re-litigate — plan around these)

### D1. Outbox format

Each <|report ...|> tag in a turn writes ONE row to the member's outbox JSONL. One turn → N rows. Each row carries its own seq, id, writtenAt, kind, summary, body, replyTo, decisions, acks. The legacy 'one envelope per turn' wrapper is retired; consumers operate on rows directly.

### D2. Body partitioning

Each row's body = the prose IMMEDIATELY ABOVE that tag — between this tag and the previous tag in the same turn (or turn start if first). The full-turn message is reconstructable by concatenation but not stored as a separate field. Each row reads as a discrete checkpoint.

### D3. Delivery rule

Lead's listener watches member outboxes. Fires only when the unread tail contains ≥1 terminal-kind row (done/question/blocked). When it fires, delivers ALL unread rows up through the latest as one /crews:review-mail batch. If unread contains only progress rows, listener does NOT fire — keeps waiting.

### D4. Progress-only members

STRICT mode: a member that only ever emits kind=progress and never reaches a terminal never triggers delivery. The lead's mailbox stays empty for that member indefinitely. Operator-acceptable; the manifest's lastKind/lastSummary still update so /list-members shows current activity. If the lead needs to peek at a progress-only trail on demand, they can run /crews:read-member <name> --all.

### D5. Mail-resolution attributes (replyTo / acks / decisions)

Per-row. Each row carries its own replyTo/acks/decisions. The lead's reviewed-cursor advances across the whole delivered batch and credits any row in the batch that resolved an incoming message (matches today's findCurrentDecision semantics, just iterated over multiple rows).

### D6. Body-canonical hard-block

Applied per terminal row (unchanged semantics, just multi-row). If a terminal row has summary > limit AND body < floor, that row is rejected at Stop-hook time. Progress rows exempt as today. A turn with multiple terminal rows where ANY one fails body-canonical → the turn fails; member must re-emit.

## Surface inventory (rough — plan should refine)

- hooks/mailbox.js — rewrite parseTurnTags to extract per-tag blocks with their owning body slice; new outbox-row writer that appends N rows instead of one envelope
- hooks/stop.js — emit per-tag rows; per-row body-canonical detection on terminal rows
- hooks/listener-loop.js + lib/listener-loop.js — terminal-gated batch fire (today fires on any new row)
- hooks/commands/review-mail.js — return multi-row batches in entries[]; cursor semantics across multi-row delivery
- hooks/commands/read-member.js — multi-row return; back-compat with --peek / --since / --all

command.name: crews-inner-pid-capture-not-firing
command.descriptionHtml: Brainstorm-first. The v1.9.2 Node-side WMI inner-PID capture (commit f8cdcc90, designed to write the inner Copilot/Claude CLI PID to disk asynchronously so that stop-member can hard-terminate cleanly and let wt close the tab) is empirically NOT firing for Copilot-engine members on this dev box. Observed 2026-05-30 across 3 stop-member calls (G impl, plan-protocol-v2, others): every call returned refusedReason: "inner-pid-missing", fell back to force-killed-fallback on the launcher pwsh, and likely left wt tabs as [process exited] placeholders. The v1.9.2 ship was operator-empirically-validated when it shipped, but those validations may have used a Claude-engine member; the regression is Copilot-specific. Brainstorm should pressure-test where the capture is failing (capture child never spawns? WMI lookup doesn't find Copilot CLI process? backoff times out? wrong CommandLine-marker pattern matched against Copilot's actual command line shape?), and propose a diagnostic + fix path.

warnings.html: ⚠️ Regression in v1.9.2 hard-terminate path for Copilot-engine members. The v1.9.2 inner-PID capture is foundational to the clean-tab-close UX — without it, hard-terminate silently regresses to v1.9.1's force-kill-fallback behavior. Brainstorm should reproduce on a dedicated test spawn (capture diagnostic output: was spawnInnerPidCapture called? did it find a child PID? what was the WMI Query that ran? what was Copilot CLI's actual CommandLine?), then propose either a marker-injection fix (stamp a unique env-var into the wt.exe new-tab command so WMI lookup can find the process by a guaranteed-unique substring) or an alternative mechanism (e.g., have the spawned shell write its own PID to disk on first turn via a SessionStart hook).

prompts.brainstorm:
/brainstorm-with-ralph "Why is the v1.9.2 Node-side inner-PID capture not firing for Copilot-engine members on this dev box?

## Empirical evidence (operator-observed 2026-05-30)

Three stop-member calls today, all targeting Copilot-engine members in crew ralph-pipeline:

1. impl-ralph-overview-data-relocation-job2 (sessionId e88aa330) → terminationKind:'hard', innerCli:null, descendants:[7 PIDs], launcherPwsh:{pid:95612, fate:'force-killed-fallback'}, wtServerPid:32460, refusedReason:'inner-pid-missing'
2. plan-crews-protocol-v2-per-report-outbox (sessionId 50060731) → terminationKind:'hard', innerCli:null, descendants:[7 PIDs], launcherPwsh:{pid:79620, fate:'force-killed-fallback'}, wtServerPid:32460, refusedReason:'inner-pid-missing'
3. Earlier in-session smoke tests (sessions in conversation logs) had the same pattern.

In every case the WMI capture child wrote no inner.pid; stop-member fell back to force-killing the launcher pwsh; tabs likely persisted as '[process exited]' placeholders rather than closing cleanly.

v1.9.2 (commit f8cdcc90) was supposed to fix this exact regression for v1.9.1. The fix uses a Node-side background PowerShell capture child that does parent-of process scanning to find Copilot CLI's PID asynchronously after spawnMember returns. The fact that it's failing for ALL Copilot-engine members today suggests the regression is Copilot-engine-specific (the v1.9.2 ship was validated, but possibly only against Claude-engine members).

## Design axes

### Axis 1 — Where is it failing?

A. Capture child never spawned (spawnInnerPidCapture not invoked, or invoked but the spawn failed silently)
B. Capture child spawned but the WMI query (Get-CimInstance Win32_Process | where ...) never matched any process
C. Match logic looked for a Claude-CLI-specific CommandLine pattern that doesn't match Copilot CLI
D. Backoff retried N times and timed out before Copilot CLI appeared in the process table
E. The capture wrote inner.pid to the wrong path (race condition with manifest dir creation, wrong cwd, etc.) so stop-member's lookup didn't find it

Brainstorm should propose a diagnostic plan that enumerates which of these is happening on this box.

### Axis 2 — Diagnostic mechanism

A. Add verbose logging to spawnInnerPidCapture + the WMI query and re-run a test spawn
B. Capture the actual Copilot CLI CommandLine on this box (Get-WmiObject Win32_Process | Where {$_.Name -eq 'node.exe'} | Select-Object ProcessId, CommandLine | ConvertTo-Json) and compare against the v1.9.2 marker pattern
C. Add an integration test that exercises the full v1.9.2 capture flow against a Copilot-engine spawn
D. All of the above

### Axis 3 — Fix strategy (depends on Axis 1 diagnosis)

If Axis 1 is C (wrong CommandLine pattern): update the WMI query to use a guaranteed-unique marker stamped into the wt.exe new-tab command (e.g., --title 'CREWS_CAPTURE_<uuid>') and pattern-match on title. Cross-engine, no engine-specific path.
If Axis 1 is D (timing/backoff): tune backoff, or have the inner CLI write its own PID via a SessionStart hook (more reliable than external WMI lookup).
If Axis 1 is A or B: investigate why the capture child isn't being invoked or its query isn't matching anything.
If Axis 1 is E: fix the path/race.

### Axis 4 — UX impact mitigation in the meantime

Until this fix lands, every hard-terminate likely leaves a '[process exited]' tab placeholder. Should we surface this in the stop-member output so the operator knows to manually close the tab? E.g., add a 'tab may persist; close manually with Ctrl+W' note when refusedReason='inner-pid-missing'.

### Axis 5 — Out of scope

- Replacing wt.exe with a different terminal emulator (out of scope; tracked elsewhere).
- Cross-platform support (Mac/Linux); this is Windows-only because wt is Windows-only.

## Deliverable

At end of brainstorm Phase 5, produce .ralph/brainstorms/crews-inner-pid-capture-not-firing/selected-direction.md with:
- Recommended diagnostic plan (which axis to investigate first, what data to collect)
- Recommended fix strategy (depends on diagnosis, but pre-commit to a likely path so the planner has a starting point)
- Recommended interim UX (Axis 4 — yes/no)
- Open questions for the planner
- Plugin version bump target (likely v1.9.3 if a small fix, v1.10.0 if it requires a structural change like SessionStart-hook PID-write)

Do NOT chain into /plan-with-ralph. The bookkeeper spawns a separate plan member from selected-direction.md.

command.name: crews-parser-multi-tag-stopgap
command.descriptionHtml: Plan-first stopgap. Short-term patch for the parseTurnTags first-tag-wins bug (D:/ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/crews/hooks/mailbox.js:761-767) that silently drops terminal kind tags when a Copilot member emits multiple <|report ...|> tags in one Stop-hook turn. The long-term fix is the v2.0.0 protocol bump (crews-protocol-v2-per-report-outbox) but that has 8 stories and will take days. This stopgap ships as v1.9.3 (or v1.9.x patch) and uses a minimally-invasive terminal-preference rule: pick the LAST terminal-kind (done/question/blocked) tag in the buffer; if none, pick the LAST progress; each tag's attributes (kind/summary/replyTo) stay atomic (no cross-tag attribute borrowing). This is option B from the operator brainstorm 2026-05-30 — explicitly NOT last-tag-wins (which has its own edge cases) and NOT severity-ordered. Lifetime: ships immediately, deprecated when v2.0.0 lands.

warnings.html: ⚠️ Coordinate with crews-protocol-v2-per-report-outbox. This stopgap modifies parseTurnTags in hooks/mailbox.js — the same function the v2 impl will rewrite end-to-end. Plan must explicitly handle the merge order: stopgap MUST land first; v2 impl rebases on stopgap and replaces the patched logic with the per-row implementation. Don't let the v2 impl skip past on the assumption stopgap hasn't landed yet — verify the v2 PRD references this stopgap's terminal-preference semantics as the baseline behavior its rewrite must preserve (in the multi-tag-turn migration test cases). Earlier-summary content is DISCARDED in this stopgap (atomic per-tag attributes); v2 will preserve them as per-row outbox rows.

prompts.plan:
/plan-with-ralph "Apply a stopgap patch to crews parseTurnTags (hooks/mailbox.js:761-767) that uses terminal-preference + atomic per-tag attributes to fix the silent-drop-of-terminal-kind bug observed 2026-05-30 with multi-tag Copilot turns.

## Background

Observed 2026-05-30 with impl-plan-with-ralph-auto-worktree: a Copilot member emitted 3 progress tags followed by 1 done tag in a single Stop-hook turn. Current parseTurnTags uses === null guards on kind/summary/replyTo (mailbox.js:761-767), so it locked onto the FIRST progress tag and silently discarded the done tag. The lead never saw the kind=done envelope; the member's commit SHAs + validation results were buried in seq 2's body marked kind=progress.

Long-term fix is crews-protocol-v2-per-report-outbox (8-story v2.0.0 ship). This task is a stopgap to remove the silent-drop bug in production while v2 lands.

## Locked design (operator picked 2026-05-30)

### D1. Terminal-preference, last-wins-among-terminals

Scan all <|report ...|> tags in the buffer. Pick the canonical tag by:
  1. Scan RIGHT-TO-LEFT, pick the FIRST tag whose kind ∈ {done, question, blocked}
  2. If no terminal tags exist, scan right-to-left for the FIRST tag whose kind === 'progress'
  3. If still no valid kind tag, leave kind=null (existing 'missing kind tag' Stop-hook block fires unchanged)

### D2. Atomic per-tag attributes

The chosen tag's kind, summary, replyTo are taken ATOMICALLY from THAT tag's block — no cross-tag attribute borrowing. A done tag with no summary stays summary=null even if an earlier progress had summary=\"...\".

This is explicitly NOT last-tag-wins (which would pick a stray trailing progress over an earlier terminal). NOT severity-ordered (which complicates the picking rule). NOT body-merging from earlier tags (that comes with v2.0.0 per-row rows).

### D3. ack / decision accumulation

ack/decision attributes continue to accumulate across ALL tags in the buffer (unchanged semantics — acks are about resolving incoming mail, not stating turn intent). Today's lines 768-778 in mailbox.js already iterate. Keep as-is.

### D4. Earlier-tag content is DISCARDED

Earlier progress tags' summaries do not appear in the envelope (no concatenation, no summaryHistory[]). The operator explicitly acknowledged this is acceptable for a stopgap; v2.0.0 preserves them as per-row outbox rows. Document this in the CHANGELOG.

### D5. Version bump

v1.9.3 (patch) — pure bug fix, no API change, no consumer-visible shape change (envelope still has scalar kind/summary/replyTo; just sourced from a different tag now).

## Surface

- hooks/mailbox.js — patch parseTurnTags (lines 761-767): replace === null guards with a two-pass scan (collect all tag blocks; pick winner per D1; extract winner's attributes per D2)
- hooks/protocol/report-tags.js — no change
- hooks/stop.js — no change (still consumes parsed kind/summary/replyTo as today)
- tests/protocol-report-tags.test.js — add multi-tag test cases (the table from the operator brainstorm 2026-05-30):
   - progress + progress → kind=progress, summary from SECOND progress
   - progress + done → kind=done, summary from done
   - done + progress → kind=done, summary from done (terminal wins over trailing progress)
   - question + done → kind=done, summary from done (last terminal)
   - done + question → kind=question, summary from question (last terminal)
   - done (no summary) + progress (with summary) → kind=done, summary=null (no cross-borrow)
   - <invalid-kind-tag> + done → kind=done, summary from done
   - no tags → kind=null (existing behavior)
- CHANGELOG.md — document the bug, the fix, the rationale for terminal-preference, the deprecation timeline (v2.0.0 will rewrite this whole path)
- AGENTS.md (toolkit) — no change (briefing examples still show single-tag pattern; that remains valid)
- codexu AGENTS.md crews-plugin-invariants section — note the v1.9.3 stopgap behavior alongside the v2.0.0 in-flight note

## Acceptance criteria

- parseTurnTags test suite passes with the new multi-tag cases
- All existing single-tag tests still pass unchanged
- Manual test: spawn a Copilot member with a contrived multi-tag turn; verify envelope.kind === 'done' and envelope.summary is the done tag's summary
- CHANGELOG v1.9.3 entry exists

Do NOT add reply-to=\"spawn\".

command.name: crews-orchestrator-tab-rename
command.descriptionHtml: Plan-first. When a crew lead role is assigned to an existing terminal session, rename the host wt.exe tab to ♔ <name> (<crew>) — mirroring the existing member-side ♙ <name> (<crew>) convention (set at spawn time via wt.exe --title + copilot --name + COPILOT_DISABLE_TERMINAL_TITLE=1). Creates a visually-coherent crew lineup (king + pawns) and makes the orchestrating tab immediately identifiable in a multi-tab Windows Terminal window. Plan must enumerate the OSC-vs-wt-rename-vs-both mechanism trade-offs (Copilot per-intent OSC writes can clobber OSC-only renames; wt.exe rename-tab persists at the OS level).

warnings.html: ⚠️ Mechanism choice matters for Copilot sessions. Members get a sticky title because v1.8.12 stamps COPILOT_DISABLE_TERMINAL_TITLE=1 on the launcher script BEFORE copilot starts. For an already-running lead session, that env-var can't be set retroactively — so OSC-emit alone may flicker as Copilot writes per-intent titles. The planner should either (A) accept the flicker, (B) use wt.exe --window 0 rename-tab "..." which takes precedence over inner-pane OSC writes, or (C) both. Empirical test on this dev box's Copilot setup is required, not a paper decision.

prompts.plan:
/plan-with-ralph "When a crew lead is assigned to an existing terminal session (via /crews-assign-role lead --crew <X> --name <Y>, or on first /crews-status if the role is auto-detected), rename the host wt.exe tab to:

    ♔ <name> (<crew>)

Mirroring the existing member-side convention (members get ♙ <name> (<crew>) stamped at wt.exe spawn time via --title, plus copilot --name + COPILOT_DISABLE_TERMINAL_TITLE=1 to keep it from being clobbered).

## Background / why

Today members are immediately identifiable by their tab title (♙ <name> (<crew>)) — operator can glance at the wt.exe window and see every crew member at a glance. The lead/orchestrator tab is whatever the operator launched (often just 'PowerShell' or the engine's per-intent OSC titles), making it hard to spot the orchestrating tab in a multi-tab Windows Terminal window. Naming the lead ♔ <name> (<crew>) closes that gap and creates a visually-coherent crew lineup (king + pawns).

## Glyph choice

♔ (white king, U+2654) for lead. Pairs thematically with ♙ (white pawn, U+2659) used for members today. Both are widely-rendered in Windows Terminal default fonts.

Future open question (NOT for this plan): if/when we add other crew roles (advisor, observer, etc.), what chess-piece glyphs map to them? Out of scope for v1.

## Existing member-side machinery (reference)

- D:/ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/crews/hooks/actors.js:1781 — sessionDisplayName template for new tabs (♙ <name> (<crew>))
- actors.js:1950 — tabTitle stamped via wt.exe --title at spawn
- actors.js:1822-1826 — comment chain on COPILOT_DISABLE_TERMINAL_TITLE=1 keeping the title stable for the tab lifetime
- tests/engine-field.test.js, copilot-review-fixes.test.js — existing test coverage

## Surface for THIS task (where lead-side rename happens)

- D:/ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/crews/hooks/commands/assign-role.js — likely entry point; emit rename when role transitions to 'lead'
- (Possibly) hooks/session-start.js or equivalent — emit rename on session start if role is already 'lead' from prior manifest

## Mechanism options (planner should pick one with rationale)

### Option A: OSC escape sequence at assign-time

When assign-role transitions to lead, print to stdout:

    \x1b]0;♔ <name> (<crew>)\x07

(or the equivalent \x1b]2;...\x1b\\ ST-terminated form). Lightweight, no shelling out, works on any wt-compatible terminal.

Risk: Copilot's per-intent OSC title updates (controlled by COPILOT_DISABLE_TERMINAL_TITLE) may clobber the title we set, the same way they did for members until v1.8.12 added the env-var workaround. But we can't stamp COPILOT_DISABLE_TERMINAL_TITLE on an already-running copilot — that's a startup env-var. So Option A alone may flicker.

### Option B: wt.exe rename-tab subcommand

Shell out to:

    wt.exe --window <current> rename-tab "♔ <name> (<crew>)"

This persists better because wt.exe owns the tab title at the OS level (overrides per-process OSC writes from inside the pane). Downside: requires identifying the current wt window-id (use --window 0 to target the active one), and the tab-rename API may not be available on older wt.exe versions.

### Option C: Both A and B

Emit OSC first (immediate update), then call wt-rename as a follow-up to lock it in. Belt-and-suspenders; small overhead.

### Option D: Just document the limitation; don't auto-rename

Punt. Operator manually renames their tab. (Rejected by operator-requested task scope, but plan should note this as the no-fix baseline.)

Recommended: planner picks A, B, or C with empirical testing on this dev box's Copilot setup. C is likely most-robust.

## Acceptance criteria

- After /crews-assign-role lead --crew <X> --name <Y> the wt.exe tab title visibly changes to '♔ <name> (<crew>)' within ~1s
- Title persists through subsequent Copilot tool calls (does not flicker back to per-intent titles)
- /crews-assign-role none (clearing the role) restores the original title (best-effort; OK if it just leaves the last set title rather than the original)
- Existing member-side tab renaming (♙ prefix) is untouched
- One unit test confirms the rename emit-path is invoked when role transitions to lead
- Manual smoke test recorded in CHANGELOG: spawn a fresh Copilot session, run /crews-assign-role lead, screenshot or transcript of the renamed tab

## Edge cases for plan to address

- Operator launches Copilot in a non-wt.exe terminal (PowerShell ISE, ConEmu, raw conhost). OSC may still work; wt-rename will silently fail. Plan should not crash in those cases.
- Lead session is started via /crews-resume-crew or auto-detected from prior manifest on SessionStart — title should still be set then, not only on the assign-role command.
- Operator renames the tab manually after assign — do we re-clobber on next heartbeat, or respect operator intent? Plan should pick a policy (likely: only emit on role transitions, not on every heartbeat).

## Out of scope

- Cross-platform (mac/Linux iTerm/gnome-terminal title sequences). Windows-only as members are.
- New crew roles beyond lead/member. King-and-pawn is the v1 set.
- Customizable glyph (operator override). Hard-coded ♔ for now.

## Background

Observed 2026-05-29 across three plan-spawn cycles (codexu-bin-ralph-overview-wrapper-retirement, crews-stop-member-hard-terminate-no-envelope x2, ralph-overview-data-relocation-and-json-migration) that /plan-with-ralph does NOT manage its own worktree. Each plan member had to be instructed via the bookkeeper-lead's spawn-prompt to create a worktree manually, e.g.:

```
WORKTREE MANDATE: use `git worktree add ../codexu-plan-<slug> -b ralph/plan-<task-id> main` and do ALL work inside that worktree.
```

That's bookkeeper-side toil per spawn AND a source of bugs:
- Three sibling-of-repo worktrees were created in error (`../codexu-plan-wrapper-retirement`, `../codexu-plan-hard-terminate`, `../codexu-plan-hard-terminate-v2`) because the lead's spawn-prompt followed an outdated AGENTS.md pattern.
- One leftover worktree ended up at `D:/codexu-plan-data-relocation` (root of D: drive) — definitely not where any documented convention says.

Meanwhile /implement-with-ralph DOES auto-manage a worktree at `.ralph/jobs/<task-id>/worktree/` (verified from existing worktrees on codexu). The asymmetry is the bug.

## Goal

When /plan-with-ralph is invoked, the skill itself should:
1. Determine task-id from the invocation (already in scope via the spawn prompt or --from-brainstorm path).
2. Create a worktree at `.ralph/jobs/<task-id>/worktree/plan/` on a fresh topic branch `ralph/plan-<task-id>` (or `-v2`, `-v3` suffix if siblings already exist on origin — investigate edge case).
3. Do all plan work INSIDE that worktree (commit deliverables there, push the topic branch, etc.).
4. Report the worktree path + topic branch in its final kind=done message so the lead knows where to FF from and what to clean up.
5. NOT touch the lead's primary working dir (which stays on main per AGENTS.md).

## Design questions for the plan

### Q1. Worktree path: subdir or no?

   A. `.ralph/jobs/<task-id>/worktree/` (matches /implement-with-ralph's existing layout exactly)
   B. `.ralph/jobs/<task-id>/worktree/plan/` (with a `plan/` subdir, so if both plan + impl are open at the same time they don't conflict)
   C. `.ralph/jobs/<task-id>/worktree-plan/` (sibling-of-worktree, different basename)

   Lean toward **B**: subdir lets the plan worktree coexist with a future impl worktree at `.ralph/jobs/<task-id>/worktree/impl/`. Plan should verify whether /implement-with-ralph would conflict with a same-task worktree dir already existing.

### Q2. Topic branch naming and v2/v3 collision

If the lead re-spawns a plan member after the first one shipped (e.g., the v2 case observed 2026-05-29 where the plan was corrected based on operator feedback), the topic branch `ralph/plan-<task-id>` already exists on origin. Strategies:

   A. Skill detects the collision and auto-suffixes `-v2`, `-v3`, etc. (what member B did manually for the hard-terminate task)
   B. Skill fails fast and requires the lead to delete the old branch first
   C. Skill always uses a UUID/timestamp suffix

   Lean toward **A** (auto-suffix). Matches what already happened organically in the smoke-test session.

### Q3. Cleanup story

Who cleans up the plan worktree + topic branch after the lead FF's?

   A. Lead does it manually (current state, post-FF cleanup is bookkeeper toil)
   B. Skill provides a 'plan-complete' subcommand the lead can run after FF that nukes both
   C. Skill auto-detects post-FF state on next invocation (e.g., the worktree's branch HEAD is reachable from origin/main → safe to remove)

   Lean toward **B** (explicit subcommand) — cleanest API. The lead's post-FF flow becomes: `git merge --ff-only <sha> && git push origin main && /plan-with-ralph cleanup <task-id>`.

### Q4. Sequencing with the existing /implement-with-ralph skill

/implement-with-ralph uses `.ralph/jobs/<task-id>/worktree/`. If Q1 picks A (same path for plan and impl), there's a collision if both phases are active. If B (with `plan/` subdir), need to also rename impl's worktree to `impl/` subdir for symmetry — that's a breaking change for /implement-with-ralph. Plan should think about whether to:

   - Migrate both skills together (synchronized rename)
   - Keep /implement-with-ralph at `.ralph/jobs/<task-id>/worktree/` and put /plan-with-ralph at `.ralph/jobs/<task-id>/worktree-plan/` to avoid the symmetry burden
   - Some other naming scheme

## Reference

- `D:/ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/ralph-orchestration/skills/plan-with-ralph/SKILL.md` (or wherever the plan-with-ralph skill body lives) — current behavior, no worktree auto-management.
- `D:/ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/ralph-orchestration/skills/implement-with-ralph/SKILL.md` — reference for how the impl skill manages its worktree (the design to mirror).
- `D:/harness-efforts/codexu/AGENTS.md` 'Branch + worktree discipline' section — codified worktree-placement convention (2026-05-29 update); this task's deliverable should match.
- Smoke-test session 2026-05-29: three plan-member spawns that each needed manual worktree mandates in the spawn prompt; one cleanup miss at `D:/codexu-plan-data-relocation`.

## Phase discipline + reporting

This is the PLAN phase. Produce ONLY a plan deliverable. Do NOT chain into impl.

COMMIT TARGET: lead is on `main`. Create a worktree at `.ralph/jobs/ralph-orchestration-plan-with-ralph-auto-worktree/worktree/plan/` (eating our own dog food — use the convention this task is establishing). Commit on `ralph/plan-ralph-orchestration-plan-with-ralph-auto-worktree`, push to `origin`, report commit SHA + branch + worktree path in kind=done body.

REPORTING (crews v1.8.x body-canonical hard-block): final turn ends with `<|report kind=\"done\" summary=\"<short>\"|>`. Substantive content (commit SHA, branch, worktree path, picked options Q1-Q4, open questions, anomalies) in PROSE BODY. DO NOT add `reply-to=\"spawn\"`."

command.name: ralph-overview-init-consumer-cross-engine-wrapper
command.descriptionHtml: Brainstorm-first. Push cross-engine plugin-path awareness UPSTREAM into the ralph-overview plugin's scripts/init-consumer.mjs so every consumer (codexu and future consumers alike) gets a working pnpm sync-ralph-state / pnpm overview under BOTH Claude Code and Copilot CLI without each consumer needing to hand-roll a per-repo resolver wrapper. Companion to the codexu-side fix codexu-bin-ralph-overview-wrapper-retirement (plan @ commit e527f83e, impl shipped 2026-05-29) which un-ignored + committed codexu's existing wrapper as a SHORT-TERM measure — this task is the long-term ecosystem fix. Option C1 from the plan: overview-init emits a tiny consumer-side wrapper file at install time AND package.json scripts that point at node bin/ralph-overview.mjs <sub> instead of the current $CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT-only form. The wrapper is plugin-versioned (consumers run overview-init --force after a plugin upgrade to refresh it) and the plugin can ship unit-test coverage of every install-layout (Claude versioned cache, Copilot single-copy, env-var override, local-dev fallback) — something codexu's hand-rolled wrapper currently lacks.

warnings.html: ⚠️ Cross-engine surface (Claude Code AND Copilot CLI install layouts). Brainstorm should pressure-test how consumers absorb the wrapper-bump on plugin upgrade — is overview-init --force idempotent? Does it preserve consumer-side customizations? What's the migration story for codexu (which today has a hand-committed wrapper that will conflict with the plugin-emitted one)? Target plugin version bump: v2.5.0+ minor. prompts.brainstorm:
/brainstorm-with-ralph "Push cross-engine plugin-path resolution UPSTREAM into the ralph-overview plugin's overview-init skill so every consumer gets a working pnpm sync-ralph-state + pnpm overview under BOTH Claude Code AND Copilot CLI, without each consumer hand-rolling a per-repo resolver wrapper.

## Why this matters

The ralph-overview plugin's current `scripts/init-consumer.mjs` (./ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/ralph-overview/scripts/init-consumer.mjs lines 10-15) emits PACKAGE_SCRIPTS of the form `node $CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT/ralph-overview/bin/ralph-overview.mjs <sub> --repo .`. Those scripts break on Copilot CLI because Copilot exports NO equivalent env var (verified 2026-05-29 against https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/copilot-cli-reference/cli-plugin-reference — Copilot exposes only COPILOT_AGENT_SESSION_ID, COPILOT_CLI, COPILOT_CLI_BINARY_VERSION, COPILOT_LOADER_PID, COPILOT_RUN_APP, COPILOT_HOME).

Codexu worked around this with a hand-rolled `bin/ralph-overview.mjs` wrapper that probes both engine install paths. That wrapper has now been committed (task `codexu-bin-ralph-overview-wrapper-retirement`, plan @ commit `e527f83e`, impl shipped 2026-05-29) as a SHORT-TERM fix — but every NEW consumer of the plugin would have to author the same wrapper themselves. The long-term fix is to push the resolution UPSTREAM into the plugin.

Reference: codexu's `bin/ralph-overview.mjs` (now tracked in the codexu repo) is the working reference implementation of the cascade — it's ~130 LoC, self-contained, and has been battle-tested 2026-05-29 against Copilot CLI install + env-override + local-dev fallback (see `.ralph/jobs/codexu-bin-ralph-overview-wrapper-retirement/smoke-test.md`). The plugin-side version would be ~identical but unit-tested.

## Design axes to pressure-test

### Axis 1 — Where does the wrapper live in the consumer repo?

A. **`bin/ralph-overview.mjs` in the consumer repo** (matches codexu's current pattern). Pro: simple, discoverable, matches what package.json scripts already say. Con: consumer repo now ships a generated file that's tracked in git; regenerating on plugin upgrade requires explicit `overview-init --force` step.
B. **`scripts/ralph-overview.mjs`** instead of `bin/`. Same trade-offs but avoids any `/bin/` gitignore-by-convention concerns (codexu had to un-ignore `/bin/` to make this work; other consumers may have similar global gitignore rules).
C. **Inline in `package.json` scripts** via `node -e "...resolver code..." <sub>`. Pro: zero tracked files. Con: cross-shell quoting hell on Windows + cmd + PowerShell + bash; long inline strings are unreadable and hard to debug.
D. **Install into `node_modules/.bin/ralph-overview`** as a postinstall step. Pro: matches npm/pnpm convention. Con: requires the plugin to ship as an npm package or have a postinstall hook that pnpm runs reliably across both engine installs.

Lean toward **A** (matches codexu's existing layout, minimal surprise). But brainstorm should weigh B vs A for new consumers without legacy.

### Axis 2 — Cross-engine install-path cascade

The wrapper must probe (at least) these install layouts:
1. `$RALPH_OVERVIEW_PLUGIN_ROOT` env override (escape hatch for plugin-dev)
2. `$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT/<plugin>/` (Claude Code harness-set)
3. `$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT/cache/<marketplace>/<plugin>/<latest>/` (Claude Code cache)
4. `~/.claude/plugins/cache/<marketplace>/<plugin>/<latest>/` (Claude Code user install)
5. `~/.copilot/installed-plugins/<marketplace>/<plugin>/` (Copilot CLI user install, no per-version subdir)
6. Local-dev fallback? (codexu has one at `./ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/ralph-overview/` — should the plugin-emitted wrapper include any local-dev escape, or rely on RALPH_OVERVIEW_PLUGIN_ROOT for plugin-author iteration?)

Brainstorm should decide on the canonical cascade order + whether to expose any plugin-side configuration of additional probe paths.

### Axis 3 — `overview-init` API for the new emit

Current `initConsumer({addPackageJsonScripts: true})` writes scripts only. New shape options:

A. **Additive flag:** `addPackageJsonScripts: true, addConsumerWrapper: true` (default both true).
B. **Single flag rename:** rename to `addPackageJsonScriptsAndWrapper: true` to signal the new bundled emission.
C. **Subcommand split:** `overview-init` is now always-bundled; add `overview-init --wrapper-only` and `overview-init --scripts-only` for advanced cases.

Lean toward **A** (additive flag, both default true). Existing consumers calling `addPackageJsonScripts: true` should opt in to `addConsumerWrapper: true` explicitly the first time, to avoid surprise file creation.

### Axis 4 — Migration story for codexu (the current consumer with a hand-committed wrapper)

Codexu's `bin/ralph-overview.mjs` is now tracked. When this plugin task ships v2.5.0+ with the auto-emit feature, codexu can:

A. Re-run `overview-init --force` to replace its hand-committed wrapper with the plugin-emitted one (and stay in sync with future plugin upgrades automatically).
B. Keep its hand-committed wrapper indefinitely; never opt into the auto-emit feature.
C. Run `overview-init --diff` first to see what would change, then decide.

Plan should document the recommended migration path for codexu + any other consumers that may exist by then.

### Axis 5 — Test coverage of every install layout

The plugin-side wrapper SHOULD ship with unit tests that simulate each install layout. The codexu hand-rolled wrapper has zero tests today — this is one of the long-term wins of pushing it upstream. Test cases at minimum:

- `RALPH_OVERVIEW_PLUGIN_ROOT` set to a valid path → resolves to it
- `RALPH_OVERVIEW_PLUGIN_ROOT` set to an invalid path → warns + falls through
- `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` set with direct subdir → resolves to it
- `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` set with cache versioned subdirs → picks latest by lexical sort
- `~/.claude/plugins/cache/...` versioned subdirs → picks latest
- `~/.copilot/installed-plugins/...` single dir → resolves to it
- All cascade misses → exits 2 with the friendly install-instruction message
- Found install missing the dispatcher file → exits 3
- `--repo` arg present → preserved; absent → defaulted to `gitRepoRoot()`

### Axis 6 — Out of scope for this brainstorm (separate concerns)

- The Copilot CLI plugin-install dependency-installation gap (the 2026-05-29 smoke test found `~/.copilot/installed-plugins/.../ralph-overview/` lacks `node_modules/`). That's a Copilot CLI / plugin-publish-pipeline issue, NOT something the wrapper can fix — the wrapper successfully dispatches to the install path; it's the install that's incomplete. Surface as a separate plugin-author followup if not already tracked.
- Option D from the codexu-side plan (Copilot CLI feature request for per-plugin env-var parity with `$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT`). Out of band; pursued via GitHub issue.

## Deliverable

At end of brainstorm Phase 5, produce `.ralph/brainstorms/ralph-overview-init-consumer-cross-engine-wrapper/selected-direction.md` with:

- Recommended wrapper location (A/B/C/D from Axis 1).
- Final cascade order + whether to support plugin-side configurable additional probe paths.
- Recommended `overview-init` API shape (A/B/C from Axis 3).
- Recommended codexu migration path (Axis 4).
- Test plan outline (Axis 5).
- Plugin version bump target (v2.5.0 minor candidate, or other).
- Open questions for the planner.

Do NOT chain into /plan-with-ralph. The bookkeeper spawns a fresh plan-ralph-overview-init-consumer-cross-engine-wrapper member from the selected-direction.md per phase discipline.

## Reference

- `.ralph/jobs/codexu-bin-ralph-overview-wrapper-retirement/plan.md` (commit `e527f83e`) — the parent plan that recommended this task as Option C1.
- `.ralph/jobs/codexu-bin-ralph-overview-wrapper-retirement/smoke-test.md` — empirical evidence the codexu wrapper works under Copilot CLI.
- `D:/harness-efforts/codexu/bin/ralph-overview.mjs` (committed during impl of the parent task) — the working reference implementation to port upstream.
- `./ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/ralph-overview/scripts/init-consumer.mjs` — the plugin file to modify; current PACKAGE_SCRIPTS constant at lines 10-15.
- `./ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/ralph-overview/bin/ralph-overview.mjs` — the plugin's own bin dispatcher (self-locating; reference for what env vars the plugin's runtime expects)."

prompts.brainstorm: /brainstorm-with-ralph "Make the ralph-overview snapshot that agents read (via MCP overview_parallel_ready_tasks and .ralph-overview/generated/snapshot.json) reliably FRESH, so the bookkeeper never plans a batch from stale data. Observed 2026-06-06: the MCP returned 40 ready tasks, 28 already merged/archived, and omitted same-day filings — because the snapshot is only regenerated by a watcher/one-shot sync that was not running. Design axes: (1) MCP SYNC-ON-READ — snapshot-consuming tools run a fast sync, or derive lifecycle directly from data.json + .ralph/jobs job-state, before answering; weigh latency (a full sync was ~17s here — too slow per-call; a lifecycle-only read from data.json would be fast and is exactly what the bookkeeper needs: tracked/merged/archived). (2) MCP SERVER OWNS THE WATCHER — launch/keep a chokidar watcher alive for the session so the snapshot stays current. prompts.plan:
/plan-with-ralph "Add a listener-armed invariant check to the crews Stop hook.

## Problem

Observed 2026-05-27 in the overview-bookkeeper session: when the Stop hook forces a synchronous review-mail (because lastReviewRequiredSeq > lastReviewedSeq), the cursor advances and the unreviewed-mail gate clears. If the agent then ends its turn with a text-only response (no further tool calls), the Stop hook accepts the turn-end and the listener is NOT re-armed. The next inbound message arrives with no watcher attached. The PreToolUse hook only re-arms when the agent attempts a tool call, so the gap persists until the agent acts on its own initiative.

This is symmetric to the bug the crews-review-mid-turn-v160 task was fixing (mid-turn review-required not enforced) but on the Stop side: 'turn-end without armed listener' should be blocked, just like 'turn-end with unreviewed mail' is blocked today.

## Fix

In `plugins/crews/hooks/stop.js`:

1. Read the actor's manifest.json `listenerState` field (canonical source — same field the PreToolUse hook reads).
2. If `listenerState !== 'armed'` (i.e. 'exited', 'unknown', missing, or stale per heartbeat), emit the same exit-code-2 blocking-error pattern used elsewhere:
   ```
   ReviewRequiredError: turn-end without armed listener for name \"<name>\" (crew=\"<crew>\").
   
   Run this Bash tool call now:
     command: node '<plugin>/tools/crews.js' arm --name <name> --crew <crew> --cwd <cwd> --session-id <session-id>
     run_in_background: true
   ```
   (Use the v1.6.0+ `crews.js arm` form, NOT the deprecated `wait-for-message.js`.)
3. Honor the existing v1.6.0 progress-envelope exemption — Stop hook should NOT block when the actor has only emitted a `kind=progress` envelope and there's no inbound mail expected (otherwise every progress-only turn would forever require a listener). The check should fire when:
   - The actor's role is `lead` OR `member` (any active actor).
   - The kind tag is one of `done`, `question`, `blocked` (terminal-ish kinds expect a sender response).
   - OR the actor has pending outbound messages awaiting reply (queueDepth > 0 in mailbox audit).

## Files to touch

1. `ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/crews/hooks/stop.js` — the fix.
2. `ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/crews/CLAUDE.md` (and copilot-plugin/agents-plugin mirrors) — document the new Stop-hook invariant.
3. `ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/crews/tests/stop-decision.test.js` — extend with a 'unarmed-after-sync-review-mail' fixture asserting the block.
4. `ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/crews/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` + version bump (v1.6.2).
5. `ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/crews/CHANGELOG.md` — v1.6.2 entry.

## Acceptance

- AC-1: After a synchronous review-mail that advances the cursor, if the agent attempts to end the turn WITHOUT an armed listener, the Stop hook emits the canonical block error containing the exact arm command.
- AC-2: A turn that ends with `kind=progress` AND zero pending outbound replies passes the Stop hook without listener-state check (no false-positive nag for idle progress-only turns).
- AC-3: A turn that ends with `kind=done` / `question` / `blocked` REQUIRES an armed listener — the actor is expected to await the orchestrator's response.
- AC-4: stop-decision.test.js adds 3 fixtures: kind=done unarmed (BLOCKED), kind=progress unarmed (OK), kind=done unarmed + queueDepth=0 (BLOCKED).
- AC-5: Existing Stop-hook tests (missing kind, unreviewed mail, strict-ack) still pass.
- AC-6: Cross-plugin coexistence still OK (agent-peers + other plugins not affected).

## Workflow

Concrete enough to skip /brainstorm-with-ralph. Run /plan-with-ralph directly. Probably decomposes into 3 stories (hook check + tests + docs+version). Phase 5a/5b internal.

Version bump: v1.6.2 (patch — defensive invariant addition). Branch + multi-remote push (Evyatar108 + gim-home)."

prompts.plan:
/plan-with-ralph "Fix the codex-exec.mjs spawn-without-shell bug in ai-developer-toolkit's ralph-orchestration plugin.

## Problem

`ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/ralph-orchestration/src/codex-exec.mjs` at v5.45.0 invokes:

```js
spawn('codex', args, { stdio: 'inherit', cwd, env })
```

Missing `shell: true`. On Windows with the Node.js CVE-2024-27980 patch (Node 18.20.5+, 20.18.1+, 22.11.0+), bare-name commands without shell context fail with ENOENT. The result: every codex iteration (and every review-changes Codex reviewer subagent) on Windows dies in ~800ms. v5.44.0 (the prior version) used a bash wrapper `codex-exec.sh` that called codex via Git Bash, so the issue didn't exist.

## Workaround in place

The impl-overview-data-dynamic-stages-schema member (running 2026-05-27) discovered the bug mid-flight. Workaround applied:

1. **Env var fallback:** Set `CODEX_EXEC_SCRIPT=C:/Users/evmitran/.claude/plugins/cache/ai-developer-toolkit/ralph-orchestration/5.44.0/codex-exec.sh` — the `resolveEngineScript` helper in v5.45 honors this and routes to the v5.44 bash wrapper.
2. **In-place patch:** Edited the cached v5.45.0 `src/codex-exec.mjs` to add `shell: true` to the spawn call, so review-changes subagents (which spawn their own ralph-orchestration instances) also work.

Auto-memory: `feedback_codex_exec_v545_windows_spawn` documents both.

## Fix

In `ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/ralph-orchestration/src/codex-exec.mjs`:

```diff
- spawn('codex', args, { stdio: 'inherit', cwd, env })
+ spawn('codex', args, { stdio: 'inherit', cwd, env, shell: true })
```

Also audit `src/copilot-exec.mjs` and any other bare-name `spawn` calls in the Node port for the same bug. Likely applies to `codex-reviewer.mjs`, `copilot-reviewer.mjs`, etc. — anywhere v5.45 ported from a shell script to Node.

Secondary consideration: `shell: true` opens command-injection risk if any argv element is attacker-controlled. Audit how `args` is constructed. For our use case args come from prompt strings written by the orchestrator — operator-trusted — so `shell: true` is acceptable. But document the threat model explicitly in a comment near the spawn call to prevent future regressions from introducing untrusted args.

Alternative implementation: use `execFile` with the absolute path to codex (`spawnSync('where', ['codex']).stdout` resolved once at startup), avoiding shell entirely. More work but safer. Plan should evaluate both and recommend.

## Files to touch

1. `ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/ralph-orchestration/src/codex-exec.mjs` — the fix (shell: true OR execFile-with-resolved-path).
2. `ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/ralph-orchestration/src/copilot-exec.mjs` — if same bug pattern, same fix.
3. `ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/ralph-orchestration/src/*.mjs` other spawn-bearing files — audit per `grep -rn spawn\(` and apply fix where applicable.
4. `ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/ralph-orchestration/CHANGELOG.md` — entry for v5.45.1 (or v5.46) with the Windows-spawn-fix note.
5. `ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/ralph-orchestration/package.json` — version bump.
6. Add a unit test (if the plugin has a test suite) that mocks spawn + asserts `shell: true` is set on Windows. If no test suite, skip.

## Acceptance

- Fix applied to all affected spawn calls in ralph-orchestration v5.45.x → v5.45.1 (or v5.46.0 if version bump policy is minor-on-fix).
- A clean install of the new version on this Windows host successfully spawns codex without the CODEX_EXEC_SCRIPT workaround.
- After fix lands and is installed, removing the workaround memory `feedback_codex_exec_v545_windows_spawn` is the lead's housekeeping job.
- Existing cross-platform behavior unchanged (Mac/Linux still work).
- Pushed to BOTH ai-developer-toolkit remotes (Evyatar108 + gim-home).

## Workflow

Concrete enough to skip /brainstorm-with-ralph. Run /plan-with-ralph directly. Probably decomposes into 2-3 stories (fix + audit + version bump + CHANGELOG). Phase 5a/5b internal to /implement-with-ralph.

Version bump: v5.45.1 (patch) — Windows-spawn-fix is strictly a bug fix, no API change."

/plan-with-ralph "Constrain Copilot CLI in research-mode invocations to read-only to prevent accidental file edits during plan-with-ralph / brainstorm-with-ralph / review-changes phases.

command.name: ralph-plan-staging-unique-path-per-member
command.descriptionHtml: Surfaced by plan-crews-lead-suppress-kind-tag (2d31eb4a) on 2026-05-28: when two plan-phase members run concurrently in the same crew, they share a staging directory at <JOBS_BASE>/.staging/<session_id>/ — but the session_id slug uses second-granularity timestamps, so two members spawning within the same second collide and overwrite each other's feature-request.txt. The concurrent member overwrote the staging mid-Phase-2; the affected member recovered by switching to a uniquely-suffixed staging path. Fix: include member-name in the staging-dir slug, OR use a millisecond/PID suffix.

prompts.plan:
/plan-with-ralph "Make ralph plan-with-ralph / brainstorm-with-ralph staging directories unique-per-member to prevent same-second collision when multiple plan members spawn concurrently in the same crew.

## Problem

Observed 2026-05-28 during 3 concurrent plan-member spawns in the overview-bookkeeper crew: plan-crews-envelope-body-canonical-for-all-kinds and plan-crews-lead-suppress-kind-tag both happened to spawn within the same wall-clock second and write to overlapping staging paths. The later member overwrote the earlier one's feature-request.txt mid-Phase-2, causing the earlier's Codex+Copilot research to receive corrupt content. The earlier member recovered by switching to a uniquely-suffixed path, but the recovery wasn't free.

## Root cause

The staging path is computed as <JOBS_BASE>/.staging/<session_id>/ where session_id is a bare timestamp slug at second-granularity. Two members spawning within the same second produce the same slug.

## Fix options

(a) Append member-name (kebab-case) to the slug: <JOBS_BASE>/.staging/<timestamp>-<member-name>/
(b) Append PID: <JOBS_BASE>/.staging/<timestamp>-<pid>/
(c) Append nanosecond timestamp: <JOBS_BASE>/.staging/<timestamp-ns>/
(d) Add random suffix: <JOBS_BASE>/.staging/<timestamp>-<random4>/

Recommended: (a) for human-readability + uniqueness.

## Acceptance

- Two plan-with-ralph members spawning within the same wall-clock second produce distinct staging paths.
- Test fixture demonstrates the collision-free guarantee.
- CHANGELOG cites the failure pattern.

Version bump: ralph v5.46.3 patch (could bundle with ralph-plan-with-ralph-copilot-cli-read-only-research). Multi-remote push."

command.name: crews-envelope-body-canonical-for-all-kinds
command.descriptionHtml: Codify a protocol contract: for ALL review-surfacing kinds (done, question, blocked — and arguably progress), the substantive content MUST live in the prose body, NOT in the summary attribute. Summary is a quick-look ≤120 chars; body is canonical. The bookkeeper-lead's mailbox-history.jsonl audit trail is supposed to preserve the full member intent for forensics — today a member can stuff the actual question into the summary attribute (as happened with impl-ralph-overview-watcher-consumer-workspace-root's rebase-auth question on 2026-05-28) and the body becomes an ack stub, defeating the audit. Combination of docs clarification + Stop-hook enforcement (warn or error when summary length exceeds N and body length is below M).

warnings.html: ⚠️ Composite task with both docs + enforcement axes. Plan member should decide: (a) docs-only — clarify SessionStart briefing + CLAUDE.md without enforcement; (b) warn enforcement — Stop-hook emits a warning to the agent transcript when summary > 200ch AND body < 50ch; (c) hard enforcement — Stop-hook BLOCKS turn-end with a 'put your content in the body, not the summary attribute' message; (d) auto-promote — when summary > N chars and body is shorter, copy summary to body automatically before envelope write. Option (c) is symmetric to the v1.6.2 listener-arm gate; option (a) is lightest-touch; option (d) is most forgiving but masks the protocol mistake.

prompts.plan:
/plan-with-ralph "Codify and enforce the crews protocol contract that the prose body carries canonical content for all review-surfacing kind tags (done, question, blocked, possibly progress) — not the summary attribute.

## Why

Observed 2026-05-28 in overview-bookkeeper coordination: a member (impl-ralph-overview-watcher-consumer-workspace-root) emitted kind=question with a 600-char summary attribute carrying the full question content + body = 'Adding the ack for the prior operator authorization message' (a 55-char ack stub). The bookkeeper lead received only the ack stub in review-mail because:

1. The summary attribute should have been ≤120 chars per SessionStart briefing.
2. The substantive content belongs in the prose body, not the summary attribute.
3. The summary-drop bug (separately tracked at crews-review-mail-summary-payload-fallback) compounded the impact, but even without that bug, the audit trail in mailbox-history.jsonl would have only had the ack stub as the searchable / human-readable record of what the member was actually asking.

The operator's directive: ALL kind values that propagate to the lead's review queue (done, question, blocked, and arguably progress) should carry the substantive content in the body, mirroring the existing kind=done convention that members already follow. The summary attribute remains a quick-look for the manifest's lastSummary field.

## Design space

### Axis 1 — Documentation

Clarify in:
- SessionStart briefing prose (the long instructions every new session reads at startup) — explicit 'body is canonical for X kinds' line.
- crews/CLAUDE.md operator manual.
- crews/docs/protocol.md if it exists; otherwise add one.
- copilot-plugin mirrors.

### Axis 2 — Enforcement (Stop-hook detection)

When a member emits a kind tag with summary attribute > N chars AND body < M chars, the Stop hook can:

**(a) docs-only** — no Stop-hook change; rely on operator + bookkeeper to flag misuse.
**(b) warn** — Stop hook emits a transcript-visible warning ('your summary attribute is long but your body is short; the audit trail will only have the body. Consider moving the content into the body before the tag.') without blocking the turn. Member sees but may proceed.
**(c) hard block** — Stop hook BLOCKS turn-end with an actionable message. Member must restructure prose before stop succeeds. Symmetric to the v1.6.2 listener-arm gate.
**(d) auto-promote** — when summary > N and body < M, the envelope-writer copies summary to body before persistence. The member's intent is preserved without operator intervention; the protocol mistake is silently corrected.

Thresholds N (summary cap above which we suspect content-stuffing) and M (body floor below which we suspect ack-only). The audit member observed N=600 / M=55 in the reproducer; plausible defaults: N=200, M=50.

### Axis 3 — Which kinds get enforcement?

- All of {done, question, blocked} — these are the review-required kinds.
- progress is more nuanced: idle progress envelopes legitimately have short bodies; enforcement here would create false positives.

Plan should evaluate whether progress envelopes need the same treatment, given the v1.6.0 progress-envelope exemption from review-required.

## Files to touch

1. plugins/crews/hooks/stop.js — if (b), (c), or (d): the kind-tag parser captures summary/body lengths and applies the chosen action.
2. plugins/crews/hooks/lib/parse-report-tag.js (or wherever the parser lives) — capture both fields, expose for downstream check.
3. plugins/crews/CLAUDE.md + .copilot-plugin/ mirror — protocol clarification.
4. plugins/crews/hooks/SessionStart.js (or wherever the long briefing prose lives) — clarification on the body-canonical rule for {done, question, blocked}.
5. plugins/crews/tests/stop-decision.test.js — fixtures for the (b)/(c)/(d) behavior on long-summary + short-body envelopes.
6. CHANGELOG.md + version bump.

## Operator-facing open questions

1. Which option for axis 2: (a)/(b)/(c)/(d)?
2. Threshold values N + M.
3. Whether progress envelopes are in-scope or exempt.

## Acceptance

- SessionStart briefing prose clearly states 'body is canonical for kind={done, question, blocked}'.
- crews CLAUDE.md documents the rule + the thresholds.
- Stop-hook behavior matches the chosen option from axis 2.
- New tests cover the new behavior (lazy-summary detection, no false-positives on legitimate short-body progress envelopes).
- Existing tests still pass (v1.6.2 listener-arm gate, v1.7.x sessionId pointer, etc).

Version bump: v1.8.0 minor (if (c) or (d) — behavioral change) OR v1.7.4 patch (if (a) or (b) — additive). Multi-remote push. Local-main FF + push-main pattern per operator preference.

Note sequencing: this task can ship before, after, or in parallel with crews-review-mail-summary-payload-fallback (v1.7.3). They address different layers: this is producer-side discipline; that is consumer-side resilience."

command.name: crews-summary-rendering-audit
command.descriptionHtml: Brainstorm-first. Surfaced by investigate-crews-summary-drop as a forward-looking audit. Catalog every crews-plugin consumer that surfaces an envelope summary field, document which ones read top-level vs payload, and identify OTHER fields with similar producer/consumer drift (candidates: kind, replyTo, progressTail). Output is a markdown audit doc + optional follow-up tasks per drifted field.

prompts.brainstorm:
/brainstorm-with-ralph "Audit every crews-plugin consumer that reads envelope summary and catalog where the producer/consumer schema may drift on other fields.

## Why

The summary-drop bug (investigation 79752a65) was caused by a producer/consumer mismatch: hooks/stop.js writes envelopes with nested payload.summary while hooks/commands/review-mail.js reads top-level row.summary. The two were drifted apart silently. Same drift may exist on other fields (kind, replyTo, progressTail, etc).

## Investigation scope

### Phase 1 — enumerate consumers

Grep all crews-plugin code that reads an envelope summary: review-mail.js (already known), format-progress-tail.js, briefing renderer, formatOutboxEntries, /list-members view code, spawn-launchers (do any echo summary?), copilot mirror hooks/commands.

For each: document file:line of the read, top-level vs payload, and what surface it renders to.

### Phase 2 — enumerate producers

Grep all crews-plugin code that WRITES envelope summary: hooks/stop.js (already known: appendSystemMailbox vs direct send), hooks/commands/send-to-member.js, hooks/commands/send-to-thread.js, format-report-tag.js, copilot mirror hook write paths.

For each: document file:line of the write, top-level / payload / both.

### Phase 3 — find drift

For each (producer, consumer) pair: do they agree on schema? If not, that's a drift candidate.

Also check OTHER envelope fields (not just summary): kind, replyTo, decision, ack, progressTail, reviewedSeq, bodyResolution.

### Lenses

Feasibility (codex) — can the audit be automated via a one-time grep pass + diff?
Devil's-advocate — is the schema asymmetry intentional (e.g. payload IS the canonical envelope shape; top-level is a flattened convenience)? If yes, the read-path fallback is the better fix than the write-path mirror.
Simplification — could we replace the dual-path schema with a single canonical envelope type defined in TypeScript that all producers + consumers use?

## Deliverable

.ralph/brainstorms/crews-summary-rendering-audit/selected-direction.md with: catalog of (consumer file:line → reads top-level vs payload) pairs for summary; catalog of producer file:line write shapes; drift findings (which producer/consumer pairs disagree); other field surveys (kind, replyTo, progressTail, etc); recommended approach (read-fallback / write-mirror / canonical-type / hybrid); per-field follow-up tasks for the bookkeeper to add (one per drifted field)."

command.name: ralph-orchestration-followup-task-gatherer
command.descriptionHtml: Add a Phase 5.5 retrospective subagent — sibling to DSAT-analyst and skill-suggester — that captures NEW follow-up tasks emerging from a ralph impl run. Inputs: iteration log, Phase 5a/5b findings (especially wont_fix + deferred), notepad.md Open Questions, and the diff against base_branch. Output: structured JSON at .ralph/jobs/<id>/followup-suggestions.json with proposed task entries (id, scope, lifecycle: tracked, prompts.{plan|brainstorm}, rationale, sourceFinding). The lead/bookkeeper consumes the suggestions when shipping the task to backlog-grow without losing surfaced threads. Mirrors today's manual bookkeeper pattern: after each ship we surface 'should we add follow-up tasks?' — automate it.
