prompts.brainstorm: /brainstorm-with-ralph "Auto-notify the crew LEAD when a member crashes, via the existing mailbox+listener channel (no polling). Today crews has crash DETECTION but no PUSH notification: hooks/health.js getMemberHealth() classifies a member dead (launcher pid not running via isProcessAlive, OR no pid + stale heartbeat past HEARTBEAT_STALE_MS), but it is pull-only -- the only callers are the list-members command (hooks/crews.js:149) and resume-crew (hooks/commands/resume-crew.js). A dead member cannot self-report (a kind=blocked report needs a live process), and the lead's armed listener only wakes on MAIL delivery, so a silent crash never wakes the lead. Observed 2026-06-06: two brainstorm members died (the UNKNOWN/-4094 lock bug, since fixed in v3.8.0) and the lead never noticed -- only the operator did, via a Copilot crash popup. The delivery plumbing already exists: appendSystemMailbox(leadName, crew, cwd, envelope, {kind}) pushes a system-sourced envelope into the lead's mailbox, which DOES wake the armed listener (it is how member-joined / member-reply / thread-fanout reach the lead). The gap is a periodic liveness sweep joining detection to delivery. PROPOSED DIRECTION (validate/refine): a listener-driven sweep that piggybacks on the lead listener's EXISTING wake cycle (idle-timeout + every delivery) -- NOT a new poll loop, honoring the always-listeners-never-poll rule -- and on an alive|quiet -> dead transition synthesizes a review-required member-crashed system envelope via appendSystemMailbox, guarded by a per-member already-notified latch in the manifest to avoid re-notifying every wake. DESIGN QUESTIONS to resolve: (1) where the sweep runs -- inside the listener subprocess just before it exits, vs at lead re-arm time in the lead model's turn; (2) a new member-crashed envelope kind (review-required) vs reusing an existing kind; (3) latch location + reset semantics on resume/clear so a resumed member can re-crash-notify; (4) false-positive avoidance (lean on the existing dead classification which already requires pid-dead or no-pid+stale-heartbeat; do NOT notify on quiet); (5) scope -- lead-only, or also surface to the operator inbox via the v3.7 operator channel? crews-scope. Reference files: hooks/health.js, hooks/mailbox.js (appendSystemMailbox), hooks/lib/listener-loop.js, and the v3.7 operator-direct channel."

STORY 1 is a hard prerequisite Phase-0 Copilot transcript probe — capture the real START / in-flight / COMPLETION event shape of a Copilot background task sub-agent and identify the stable start→done correlation key (a shellId analog); if no pre-Stop start event or stable key exists, the task collapses back to D-001 rather than shipping an unsafe detector. Filed 2026-06-06 (enhancement, not a hot bug). The progress-bg gate (hooks/stop.js ~:1167 + hooks/detect-active-bg.js) blocks a member emitting kind=progress when detection.nonListenerCount === 0. Its "active background work" detector recognizes only SHELL subprocesses (tool.execution_start with mode:async, paired with system.notification shell_completed) — NOT harness-spawned background Task/sub-agents. Observed: the arm-guard impl member, genuinely WAITING on a background Phase-5a code-review agent (a Claude Task / Copilot task sub-agent), tried to checkpoint kind=progress and was blocked because the review agent is not a shell subprocess. The member self-recovered correctly (it waited on the agent synchronously via wait: true, then reported) and concluded "the bg-gate correctly blocked an idle progress" — so this is a coarse-but-defensible behavior, NOT a hot bug. OPEN QUESTION for a brainstorm: should a pending background sub-agent count as active background work (allowing a progress checkpoint), or is forcing the member to wait synchronously the right design? If it should count, detection must be HARNESS-AWARE (recognize the engine-specific background-agent signal: Claude Task / Copilot task / codex spawn_agent) — reuse the existing harness-aware seam, do not build a runtime adapter. crews-scope.
